en: Re 31059: The eighteen ritual acts (*aṣṭādaśakriyāḥ*) and so forth— [the portions in parentheses are my suggestions based on my understanding]— are used to denote missing parts, leaf damage, or unidentified characters,
words, or letters.
Generally seven to eight lines per side of each folio;
i = image,
f = folio.
Oṃ hāṃ bhairavāya namaḥ— on the tip-joint of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Akṛta—at the middle of the base joint of the ring finger.
In the principle of Prakṛti: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kṛta—at the middle joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Brāhmaṇa—at the middle of the tip joint of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ prajeśvarāya namaḥ—on the little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ saumyāya namaḥ—on the root joint of the little finger. Oṃ hāṃ indrāya namaḥ—on the middle joint of the little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Gandharva—at the tip-joint of the little finger. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Yakṣa—at the middle joint of the base of the little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Rākṣasa—at the middle joint of the middle of the little finger.
In the earth-element (pṛthvī-tattva): *oṃ hāṃ piśācāya namaḥ* on the middle joint of the tip of the little finger;
*oṃ hāṃ sthaleśvarāya namaḥ* on the palm of the right hand;
*oṃ hāṃ sthūleśvarāya namaḥ* on the back of the palm of the right hand.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkukarṇa—at the joint at the base of the left arm. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kālājana—at the joint in the middle of the left arm.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Maṇḍaleśvara—at the tip of the joint in the middle of the left arm.
Oṃ hāṃ mahākoṭāya namaḥ—on the left thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ dviraṇḍāya namaḥ—on the first joint of the left thumb. In the principle of ego (ahaṅkāratattva): Oṃ hāṃ cchagalaṇḍāya (sakalāṇḍāya) namaḥ—on the middle joint of the left thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Gokarṇa— at the middle joint of the tip of the left thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ.
*Mahābalāya namaḥ*—on the left index finger.
*Oṃ hāṃ avimuktāya namaḥ*—on the root joint of the left index finger.
*Oṃ hāṃ rudrakoṭīśvarāya namaḥ*—in the middle of the root joint of the left index finger.
In the element of space (ākāśa-tattva): *oṃ hāṃ vastrapādāya namaḥ*—on the tip-joint of the left index finger;
*oṃ hāṃ bhīmeśvarāya namaḥ*—on the middle joint at the base of the left index finger;
*oṃ hāṃ mahendrāya namaḥ*—on the middle joint of the left index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ aṭṭahāsāya namaḥ—on the middle joint of the tip of the left index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ vimaleśāya namaḥ—on the left middle finger. Oṃ hāṃ nakhalāya namaḥ—on the base joint of the left middle finger.
Oṃ hāṃ nākhalāya namaḥ—on the middle joint of the middle finger.
Oṃ hāṃ gurukṣetrāya namaḥ—on the tip joint of the middle finger. In the element of air (vāyutatva): Oṃ hāṃ gayāya namaḥ—[on the middle joint of the ring finger].
In the middle of the base joint of the left middle finger:
*oṃ hāṃ bhairavāya namaḥ*. In the middle of the middle joint of the middle finger: *oṃ hāṃ ketārāya namaḥ*. In the middle joint of the ring finger: *oṃ hāṃ ketārāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Jalpeśvara—on the tip-joint of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śrīśaila—on the middle joint at the base of the ring finger. In the fire principle (agnitattva): Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Hariścandra—on the middle joint of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Lakulīśvara—at the middle joint of the tip of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, [salutation] to Bhābhūti.
*Namaḥ*—on the left little finger.
*Oṃ hāṃ ḍuiṇḍīmuṇḍāya namaḥ*—on the base joint of the left little finger. *Oṃ hāṃ oṣadhīśāya namaḥ*—on the middle of the base joint of the little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Prabhāsa—at the middle joint of the little finger.
For the state of impurity (apūtatva): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Amareśa—at the middle joint of the tip of the left little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vīrabhadra—at the palm of the left hand.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhadrakālī—at the back of the left hand. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Trilocana—at the joint at the base of the right foot. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Lispa (or Lpsa)—at its [the foot’s] joint.
Oṃ hāṃ nabhase namaḥ—at the morning twilight (agrāsandhyā).
Oṃ hāṃ vivāhāya namaḥ—on the toe of the right foot. Oṃ hāṃ saṃvāhāya namaḥ—on the index finger of the right foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Tridaśeśvara—with the middle fingers of the right foot. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Gaṇādhyakṣa—with the ring finger of the right foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vibhu—with the little finger of the right foot.
At the tip of the egg (aṇḍamastake): *oṃ hāṃ śambhave namaḥ*—on the upper surface of the thumb.
*oṃ hāṃ vajradaṃṣṭrāya namaḥ*—on the thick part of the thumb. *oṃ hāṃ phaṇīndrāya namaḥ*—at the first joint of the base of the right big toe.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Īśāna—on the middle joint. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Udumbara—on the tip joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Grasana—in the middle of the joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mārutāśana—at the base joint of the right foot’s index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Krodha—at the middle joint of the index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ananta—at the tip joint of the index finger.

Oṃ hāṃ viṣadharāya namaḥ—on the middle joint of the index finger. At the very bottom part: Oṃ hāṃ vṛṣāya namaḥ. On the root joint of the middle toe of the right foot: Oṃ hāṃ ba...priyāya namaḥ. On the middle joint.
Oṃ hāṃ bhūpālāya namaḥ—at the tip-joint of the [thumb]. Oṃ hāṃ sureśāya namaḥ—in the middle joint.
Oṃ hāṃ śarvāya namaḥ—at the base joint of the ring finger of the right foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Eldest—on the middle joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Supreme Veda—on the tip joint. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Arm of Knowledge—in the middle of the joint. (l. 4)
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Omniscient One—at the base joint of the little toe of the right foot. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna—at the middle joint.
Thus for Īśāna. (l. 5)
Oṃ hāṃ vidyādhipāya namaḥ—at the tip-joint. Oṃ hāṃ prakāmatāya namaḥ—at the middle of the joint.
Oṃ hāṃ prasādāya namaḥ—at the joint at the base of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śrīdhara—at the joint of the middle of the left foot. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Raktadhara—at the joint of the tip of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Lakṣmīdhara—at the big toe of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ jaṭādharāya namaḥ—on the index finger of the left foot. Oṃ hāṃ saumyadehāya namaḥ—on the middle toe of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ dhanyāya namaḥ—on the ring toe of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Rūpavat—on the left little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Nidhīśa—at the upward surface of the left big toe.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mekhalavāhana—at the base of the big toe.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Kapardin—on the first joint of the big toe of the left foot. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Pañcaśikha—on the tip joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Kṣayāntaka—on the middle joint of the left big toe.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Tīkṣṇa—at the root joint of the left index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sūkṣma—at the middle joint. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vāyuvega—at the tip joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Laghava—at the middle joint of the left index finger, in the northwest.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śīghra—at the base joint of the middle toe of the left foot. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sunādana—at the middle joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Mekhanāda—at the tip-joint. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jalāndaka—in the middle of the joint.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Dīrghabāhu—at the base joint of the ring finger of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vasahṛdaya—at the middle joint [of the thumb].
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śveta—at the tip joint. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Mahālaya—at the middle joint of the ring finger of the left foot.

Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Pāśahasta—at the root joint of the little toe of the left foot. (1.7) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Atibala—at the middle joint—in the western [direction]. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bala—at the tip joint.
Oṃ hāṃ daṃṣṭrāya namaḥ—at the middle joint of the left little toe.
Oṃ hāṃ lohitāya namaḥ. (i.5a, f.6b, l.1)
At the right hip:
*Oṃ hāṃ virūpākṣāya namaḥ*—on the right side.
*Oṃ hāṃ ūrdhvaśephāya namaḥ*—at the left hip.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Bhayānaka—on the left side. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Krūradaṇḍa—on the right shoulder.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Hantṛ—on the left shoulder.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ramaṇa—at Skanda; salutation to Nirṛti—at Nirṛti; salutation to Dharmapati—at the belly; salutation to Dharma—at the penis; Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Dharma—at the testicles.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Yoktra—at the right elbow. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Bhoktra—at the left elbow.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vidhātra—at both knees, positioned on the surface of the knees. (l. 4)
Oṃ hāṃ dhātre namaḥ—between the right eye and the inner ear. Oṃ hāṃ harāya namaḥ—between the left eye and the inner ear.
Oṃ hāṃ mṛḍave namaḥ—at the root of the right thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Yāmya—at the center of the right thigh, in the south.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kṣayāntaka—at the front of the right thigh. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhasmāntaka—at the right knee.
Oṃ hāṃ babhruve namaḥ—on the right calf.
Oṃ hāṃ dahanāya namaḥ—on the right stalk.
Oṃ hāṃ jvalanāya namaḥ—on the base of the left thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ harāya namaḥ—at the center of the left thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ khādakāya namaḥ—at the front of the left thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ piṅgalāya namaḥ—at the left knee.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Hutāśana— on the left calf.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Agnirudra—
—at the navel-stalk—on the fire [element].
*Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the Lord of the Thirty-three (*tridaśādhipa*)—at the base of the right shoulder. *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the Weapon (*śastra* or *śāstra*)—in the marrow at the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Imperishable—one at the right side of the palate (sṛśviṇi).
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vibhūti—one at the left side of the palate. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Pramardana—one on the right side of the forehead.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vajradeha—at the left side of the forehead.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vr̥dhna—at the tip of the nose. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Aja—at the middle of the eyebrows.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Kapālīśa—at the right eyebrow.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Rudra—at the left eyebrow. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu—at the root of the right eyebrow. (l. 4)
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā—at the root of the left eyebrow.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Hādaka—at the center of the right eyebrow. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kuśmāṇḍa—at the right armpit.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kālāgnirudra—on the left armpit. Thus one should place [this] within the element of earth (pṛthivī-tattva). Oṃ hāṃ aṃ, obeisance—on the head.
Oṃ hāṃ āṃ namaḥ — on the face.
Oṃ hāṃ iṃ namaḥ — on the right eye. Oṃ hāṃ īṃ namaḥ — on the left eye. (l. 6)
Oṃ hāṃ uṃ namaḥ—on the right ear.
Oṃ hāṃ ūṃ namaḥ—on the left ear. Oṃ hāṃ ṛṃ namaḥ—on the right cheek.
Oṃ hāṃ ṝṃ namaḥ—on the left cheek.
Oṃ hāṃ lṛṃ namaḥ—on the right nostril. Oṃ hāṃ lṝṃ namaḥ—on the left nostril.
Oṃ hāṃ eṃ namaḥ—to the upper lip. Oṃ hāṃ aiṃ namaḥ—to the lower lip.
Oṃ hāṃ oṃ namaḥ—to the upper teeth.
Oṃ hāṃ auṃ namaḥ— at the lower teeth. (i.6a, f.7b, l.1) Oṃ hāṃ aṃ namaḥ— at the root of the palate.
Oṃ hāṃ aḥ namaḥ—at the tip of the palate. Oṃ hāṃ kaṃ namaḥ—at the right arm.
Oṃ hāṃ khaṃ namaḥ—at the elbow of the right arm.
Oṃ hāṃ gaṃ namaḥ—at the right wrist.
Oṃ hāṃ ghaṃ namaḥ—at the palm of the right hand. Oṃ hāṃ ṅaṃ namaḥ—at the tips of the fingers of the right hand.
Oṃ hāṃ caṃ namaḥ — on the left arm.
Oṃ hāṃ chaṃ namaḥ — on the left elbow. Oṃ hāṃ jaṃ namaḥ — on the left wrist.
Oṃ hāṃ jhaṃ namaḥ on the palm of the left hand.
Oṃ hāṃ ñaṃ namaḥ on the tips of the fingers of the left hand. Oṃ hāṃ ṭaṃ namaḥ at the root of the right thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ ṭhaṃ namaḥ—on the right knee. Oṃ hāṃ ḍaṃ namaḥ—on the right shank. Oṃ hāṃ ḍhaṃ namaḥ—on the right foot.
Oṃ hāṃ ṇaṃ namaḥ—at the tips of the toes of the right foot. Oṃ hāṃ taṃ namaḥ—at the root of the thigh of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ thaṃ namaḥ—at the left knee.
Oṃ hāṃ daṃ namaḥ—on the left calf;
oṃ hāṃ dhaṃ namaḥ—on the left foot;
oṃ hāṃ naṃ namaḥ—on the tips of the toes of the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ paṃ namaḥ—on the right side. Oṃ hāṃ phaṃ namaḥ—on the left side. Oṃ hāṃ baṃ namaḥ—on the back.
Oṃ hāṃ bhaṃ namaḥ—at the navel. Oṃ hāṃ maṃ namaḥ—in the belly. Oṃ hāṃ yaṃ namaḥ—in the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ raṃ namaḥ—on the right shoulder.
Oṃ hāṃ laṃ namaḥ—on the left shoulder. Oṃ hāṃ vaṃ namaḥ—on the hip.
Oṃ hāṃ śaṃ namaḥ—on the right armpit. Oṃ hāṃ ṣaṃ namaḥ—on the left armpit.
Oṃ hāṃ saṃ namaḥ—at the ends of the right hands and feet.
Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ—at the ends of the left hand and feet.
Oṃ hāṃ ḷaṃ namaḥ—from the heart to the end of the head. Oṃ hāṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ—from the heart to the end of the feet.
In this manner, one should place the letters and the paths:
*oṃ hāṃ oṃ namaḥ* on the uppermost head.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyomavyāpin—on the eastern head.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyomarūpa—on the southern head. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sarvavyāpin—on the northern head.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva—at the western head.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ananta—at the forehead.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Anātha—at the [right] eye. (l. 3)
Oṃ hāṃ anāśritāya namaḥ—on the right eye.
Oṃ hāṃ dhruvāya namaḥ—on the left eye. Oṃ hāṃ śāśvatāya namaḥ—on the right ear.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the one established upon the yoga-seat—on the left ear.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the eternal yogin—on the right nostril. Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the one who carries away through meditation—on the left nostril.
Oṃ hāṃ oṃ namaḥ śivāya namaḥ—on the right cheek. Oṃ hāṃ sarvaprabhave namaḥ—on the left cheek.
Oṃ hāṃ śivāya namaḥ—on the face.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, the head—at the head. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, the face—at the face.
Oṃ hāṃ ambo, obeisance to the heart—at the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vāmadeva-guhyaka—at the *hu* and *hya*.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sadyojāta-mūrti—at the two feet.
Oṃ hāṃ, oṃ namo namaḥ—at the base of the right arm.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the one who is more secret than the secret—this is the midday junction (*sandhyā*) therein.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the protector.
At the wrist: *Oṃ hāṃ anidhanāya namaḥ*—at the base of the thumb. *Oṃ hāṃ sarvayogādhikṛtāya namaḥ*—in the middle of the thumb.

Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Lord of all Vidyās—on the tip of the thumb. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the one whose form is light—on the tip of the index finger. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Supreme One who is beyond the supreme lord—on the tip of the middle finger.
Oṃ hāṃ cetanācetanāya namaḥ—on the tip of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ vyomirvyomiṃ namaḥ—on the tip of the little finger. Oṃ hāṃ vyāpinvyāpiṃ namaḥ—at the base of the left arm.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Arūpin arūpin, obeisance—to the twilight in the middle of that.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the first of the first—at the wrist. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to brilliance within brilliance—at the base of the thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ jyotirjyotiṣe namaḥ—on the middle of the thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ arūpāya namaḥ—on the tip of the thumb. Oṃ hāṃ anantāya namaḥ—on the tip of the index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ adhūmāya namaḥ—at the tip of the middle finger.
Oṃ hāṃ abhasmāya namaḥ—at the tip of the ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ anādau namaḥ—at the tip of the little finger.
Oṃ hāṃ nānānānāya namaḥ—at the base of the right thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ dhūdhūdhūdhū namaḥ—at the right knee. Oṃ hāṃ bhū namaḥ—at the right shank.
Oṃ hāṃ bhuvaḥ namaḥ—on the palm of the right thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ suvaḥ namaḥ—on the middle of the right thumb. Oṃ hāṃ nidhanāya namaḥ—on the tip of the right thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Anidhana— at the tip of the right index finger. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Nidhanodbhava— at the tip of the right middle finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śiva—at the tip of the right ring finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śarva—at the tip of the right little finger. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Self—at the root of the left thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Maheśvara—at the left knee.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Mahādeva—at the left calf.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Satyabhāveśvara—at the base of the left big toe.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mahātejas—on the middle of the left thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Yogādhipati—on the tip of the left thumb.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Muñcamuñca—on the tip of the left index finger.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Prathamaprathama—on the tip of the middle finger of the left hand.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Śarvaśarva—on the tip of the ring finger of the left hand.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Bhavabhava—on the tip of the little finger of the left hand.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhavodbhava—on the left head.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the bestower of happiness upon all beings—on the left ear.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the one who causes the presence of all—on the left shoulder.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Rudra-parāya—on the left side.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Anarcita-anarcitāya—on the surface of the left hip. (l. 7) Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Astuta-stutāya—on the surface of the right hip.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Pūrvasthitapūrvasthita— on the right side.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sākṣisākṣin— (i.8a, f.9b, l.1).
On the right shoulder:
*oṃ hāṃ kurukuruve namaḥ*. On the right ear: *oṃ hāṃ pataṅgapataṅgāya namaḥ*. On the right head: *oṃ hāṃ pataṅgapataṅgāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Piṅgapiṅga—on the right shoulder.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Jñānajñāna—on the left shoulder. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śabdaśabda—on the right foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmasūkṣma—on the left foot.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva—on the right thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sarva—on the left thigh.
Oṃ hāṃ sarvadāya namaḥ—on the nose.
Oṃ hāṃ śivāya namaḥ—on the head. Oṃ hāṃ namo namaḥ—on the right arm.
Oṃ hāṃ oṃ namaḥ vāmadorbhiḥ. Thus ends the path of the words (padādhvan).
Oṃ hoṃ, obeisance to Īśāna, the head—on the head. Oṃ heṃ, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa, the face—on the face.
Oṃ huṃ, obeisance to Aghora, the heart—on the heart.
Oṃ hiṃ, obeisance to the secret of Vāmadeva—at the secret place. Oṃ haṃ, obeisance to the form of Sadyojāta—at the feet.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the heart—at the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the head—on the head.
Oṃ hūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock—on the crest-lock. Oṃ haiṃ, huṃ to the armor—in the middle of the breasts.
Oṃ hauṃ netrāya vauṣaṭ—on the eyes.
Oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ—in the four directions.
Thus one should perform the placement (nyāsa) in this sequence.
Salutations to the venerable gurus.
Salutation to the venerable Guru Dakṣiṇāmūrtti.
Homage!

(i.8b, f.11a, l.1) Having sprinkled the *śāntikumbha* with water, reciting "oṃ hrīṃ jñānaśaktyai namaḥ," and having touched the central part of the pedestal with the middle of the *kuśa* grass, one should mutter [the mantra] three times according to the number of oblations; that is the sequence.
"oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ vidyātatvābhyāṃ namaḥ vidyātatvādhipābhyām."
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutations to Jñāna and Ibhya. Then the preceptor standing by the side of the image: as follows—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāṃ, salutations to Mūrti and Ibha.
To the two presiding deities of the Earth-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhārikābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two Fire-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ vahnimūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the Fire-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dīptamatyebhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamāna-mūrti). To the two presiding deities of the forms of the Sacrificer: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two Ugras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Arka.
(To the two lords of the solar form): Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of heat.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of the watery form. To the two lords of the watery form: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two [deities] of consciousness.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Wind (vāyumūrti).
To the two lords of the forms of Wind—oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balotghaṭa and [his consort].
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Moon (indumūrti).
To the two lords of the lunar form: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are space (ākāśamūrti). To the two lords of the form of space: Oṃ hrīṃ...
"Hrīṃ, obeisance to Vibhu and Vyāpin.
Having thus worshipped, the Guru [proceeds].
"Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jñānaśakti.

Having recited this one thousand times, or five hundred, or a hundred, and having likewise recited the Brahmā-aṅgas, the Guru—having brought them into proximity by means of the Heart-mantra (hṛdaya), and having rendered them impervious and restrained by means of the Armor-mantra (varman)—should cause the Lord of the Tattvas to hear his command. To the Lord of the Vidyā-tattva, he should say: "O Knower, you who destroy the rushing faults! This seat is yours; therefore, you must remain right here through your presence."
Having thus made this request, the Guru [should then recite]:
*oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ namaḥ to the principles of Vidyā and Śiva*.
To the principles of Vidyā and Śiva—*oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ namaḥ to Knowledge and Will*.
Having thus meditated upon and performed worship, the preceptor standing beside the image [then recites]:
"Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Earth (kṣmāmūrti). Obeisance to the two presiding deities of the form of Earth. "Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two Supportresses (dhārikā)."
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrti).
To the two presiding lords of the forms of Fire: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two of radiant intellect (dīptamati).
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamāna).
To the two presiding deities of the *yajamāna-mūrti*: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ arkamūrtibhyāṃ namaḥ*. To the two presiding deities of the *arkamūrti*: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ jyotsnābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two Water-forms (jalamūrtti).
To the two lords of the Water-forms—oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ cenatābhyāṃ, salutation.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, salutation to the two Air-forms (vāyumūrtti).
To the two lords of the wind-forms (i.9b,
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balotghaṭā.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are the moon (indumūrti).
To the two presiding over the lunar forms—oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two who are Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ.
(Line 2) Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are space (ākāśamūrti).
With the two presiding deities of the form of space— *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ vibhuvyebhyāṃ namaḥ*—
having thus meditated upon and worshipped them, the Guru, who stands by the side of the [deity's] form,
goes near the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worships the fire.
For the purpose of bringing [the deity] into proximity, the Guru should first offer five oblations with the root mantra, and then:
*Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ*, salutation to the two principles of Vidyā and Śiva;
*Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ*, salutation to the two presiding deities of the principles of Vidyā and Śiva, namely Jñāna and Icchā.
Having thus performed the worship, the preceptor standing beside the image [then recites]:
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmā-mūrtibhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the Earth and the Form).
*kṣmā-mūrtty-ādhipābhyām* (To the two Lords of the Earth and the Form): *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhārikābhyāṃ namaḥ* (Salutation to the two Sustainers).
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, salutations to the two forms of Fire.
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutations to the two radiant mortals.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, salutations to the two forms of the Sacrificer.
To the two presiding deities of the Sacrifice-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ* obeisance to the two Ugras;
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ* obeisance to the two Sun-forms (*arkamūrti*). To the two presiding deities of the Sun-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ* obeisance to the two Jyotsnās.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two water-forms;
to the two lords of the water-forms: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two consciousnesses.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, salutation to the two wind-forms. (l. 8)

One should offer oblations separately with three offerings: having offered [the first] with "Oṃ hāṃ oṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the two Lords of the Principles of Knowledge and the Principle of Speech," and [the second] with "Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to Knowledge and Will.
To the two lords of the Vāyu-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ balotghaṭābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two [lords] of the Moon-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ indumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the Moon-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhātryaibhyāṃ namaḥ*. (l. 2)
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two whose forms are space (ākāśamūrti).
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two who are the lords of the form of space (ākāśamūrttyadhipa)—
having thus worshipped in the southeast (agni).
One should offer oblations separately with three offerings; this is the sequence:
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrtibhyāṃ svāhā*. To the two lords of the earth-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhātribhyāṃ svāhā*.

Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrti). To the two presiding deities of the forms of Fire: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the two [deities] of radiant intellect (dīptamati). Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamāna).
To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer (Yajamānamūrtti): Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the two Ugras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of Arka. To the two presiding deities of the form of Arka: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the two Jotsnas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, svāhā to the two embodiments of water;
to the two lords of the water-embodiments—oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the two consciousnesses;
oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, svāhā to the two embodiments of wind.
To the two lords of the Vāyu-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ balotghaṭābhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two lords of the Indu-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ indumūrttibhyāṃ svāhā*. To the two lords of the Indu-forms.

Having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, having gone [to the fire], having offered oblations, and having returned—one should perform everything as previously described. Then, for the removal of defects such as those at the root and so forth, one should offer a hundred oblations each with the *aghora* mantra and the sword-mantra (*asi*), together with the *pūrṇā*. Having given the sacrificial porridge (*caru*), having performed the final *pūrṇāhuti*, and having given water for sipping (*ācamana*) and betel leaves and the like, one should restrain Śiva, offer oblations with the *vyāhṛtis*, present the internal offering (*antarbali*), perform the salutation to the ears (*śrotravandana*), and effect the ritual integration (*sakalīkṛtya*). Having approached the presence of Śiva, one should make a formal request into the right ear of Śiva.

O Blessed One, whatever action has been performed—whether deficient or excessive—in the three parts beginning with Brahmā, through ignorance or delusion, O You who are affectionate toward Your devotees, may all that become complete here in this sacrifice by Your grace. *Oṃ*, salutations to You, the Blessed One! O Rudra, O Terrifier, salutations to You! Whether the rite is complete or incomplete, may it be fulfilled by Your power; please accept it.

Having thus made this request, having installed the *jñānaśakti*, and having restrained [it], he goes near the pedestal (*pīṭha*). Then, having requested the Goddess—“O Blessed One, may the activity in all three parts of the rite reach completion through your grace”—and having requested Śaṅkarī with “*oṃ hrīṃ śaṅkarīṃ pūraya pūraya*,” he installs the *kriyāśakti* and restrains it. Having also requested the Bull with “*oṃ hrīṃ vṛṣabhāya namaḥ*,” and having restrained the Bull as well, [he performs the rite] with burnt offerings (*homa*), the sounding of the Vedas and other [mantras], and with festivals of song, dance, and merriment.

The Guru should perform the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*) for seven nights, five nights, three nights, one night, or immediately. He should offer oblations daily with their respective mantras—one hundred oblations each—and perform worship of the *śivakumbha* and other vessels, as well as present offerings to the quarters (*dikbali*). Having consumed the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and other substances together with those bearing the forms [of the deities], he should sleep. He should sleep with the central limb [of the deity] while the mantra-holders and image-keepers are present; thereafter, the procedure for the preliminary consecration within the eighteen rites of installation (*pratiṣṭhā*) is completed.
May there be auspiciousness.
Salutations to the venerable gurus.
(i.11b, f.1a, l.1) In the upper part of Brahmā, in the portion belonging to Rudra: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Nirodha-śakti.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva-tattva.
To the Lord of the Śiva-tattva—(Oṃ Hāṃ) obeisance to Śiva. At the crown of the head—Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the Śakti-tattva. To the Lord of the Śakti-tattva—Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Śakti.
In the throat—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Sadāśiva (sadāśivatattva).
To the lord of the principle of Sadāśiva—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Īśvara (īśvaratattva).
To the Lord of the principle of Īśvara: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ananta. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Śuddhavidyā.
To the Lord of the principle of Śuddhavidyā: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śambara.
On the left side: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Māyā (māyā-tattva). To the lord of the principle of Māyā: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Gahaneśa.
On the right side, in the portion belonging to Viṣṇu: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Time (kāla-tattva).
To the Lord of the principle of time (kālatattva): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the one named Kāla. At the heart: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of necessity (niyatitattva).
To the Lord of the principle of necessity: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Restrainer (niyāmaka).
(Oṃ hāṃ) Salutation to the principle of Kalā.
To the Lord of the principle of Kalā—Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jñānabindu. (Oṃ hāṃ) Salutation to the principle of Vidyā.
To the Lord of the Principle of Knowledge: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vedic Wisdom. (l. 7) Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Principle of Passion. To the Lord of the Principle of Passion: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Kāma.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of the Puruṣa.
To the Lord of the principle of the Puruṣa—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the subtle body.
In the abdomen—(Oṃ Hāṃ) salutation to the principle of Prakṛti.
To the lord of the principle of Prakṛti—Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Pradhāna. On the back—Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Guṇa.
To the Lord of the principle of qualities (guṇatattva): Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Trideha. (L. 2) Within the center of the navel: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of intellect (buddhitattva).
To the Lord of the principle of intellect: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Buddha.
At the three joints—(Oṃ Hāṃ) salutation to the principle of *haṃ* (Haṃkāra-tattva).
To the lord of the principle of *haṃ*—Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to *haṃ*-making (Haṃkṛta).
(L. 3) In the portion of Brahmā—Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to the principle of mind (Manas-tattva).
To the lord of the principle of mind: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Saṅkalpa.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Salutation to the principle of hearing.
To the lord of the principle of hearing: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vyomacāra. (l. 4)
In the skin: *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the principle of the skin (*tvaktattva*). To the lord of the principle of the skin: *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the entire body (*sarvāṅga*).
In the eyes: *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the principle of the eye (*cakṣustattva*).
To the Lord of the Eye-principle: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Prakāśa. (L. 5) On the tongue: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Tongue-principle. To the Lord of the Tongue-principle: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mahāvaktra.

In the nose: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to the principle of the Nāsatyas (*nāsatattva*). To the lord of the principle of the Nāsatyas: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to Vilambaka. In the mouth: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to the principle of speech (*vāktattva*).
Salutation to the Lord of the principle of speech (*vāk-tattva*): *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Vibhu.
*Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the principle of the feet (*pāda-tattva*).
To the Lord of the principle of the feet: *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Ramaṇeśa. (l. 7)
In the two hands—(Oṃ Hāṃ) obeisance to the principle of the hands (pāṇitatva).
To the lord of the principle of the hands—Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the Sāmaga.
In the anus—Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the anus (pāyutatva).
To the Lord of the Pāyuta principle: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Cūrṇakṛti.
Upaste—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Upastata principle.
To the presiding deity of the genitals: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ghanānanda.
At the navel: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of sound (śabdatattva). To the presiding deity of the principle of sound: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmanāda. (Line 2)
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of touch.
To the lord of the principle of touch—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Balavaktra. (Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of form.
To the Lord of the element of form—(Oṃ Hāṃ) homage to Bhānumat. (Oṃ Hāṃ) homage to the element of taste. To the Lord of the element of taste—Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Jalada.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of smell (gandha-tattva).
To the lord of the principle of smell—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the limb of smell (gandhāṅga).
On the two yonis—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of space (ākāśa-tattva).
To the Lord of the element of space: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Sūkṣma.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the element of wind. To the Lord of the element of wind: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mātariśvan.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the fire element (agnitattva).
To the lord of the fire element—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Tviṣānidhi. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the water element (jalatattva).
Salutation to the Lord of the water element—*oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Jaleśa.
From below the knees to the feet—*oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the earth element (*pṛthivī-tattva*).
To the Lord of the earth element—*oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Śrīkaṇṭha.
Having thus performed the worship of the Tattvas and the Lords of the Tattvas, one should then install the Mūrtis and the Lords of the Mūrtis.
Then, in the portion of Guru Rudra—the Śiva-tattva: *oṃ hūṃ śivatatvāya namaḥ*;
*oṃ hūṃ śivatatvādhipataye* [namaḥ];
*oṃ hāṃ rudrāya namaḥ*.
Having performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) in this manner, the preceptor standing by the side of the image should then perform worship in the sequence starting from the east.
As follows: *Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, salutation to Kṣmāmūrti;
salutation to the Lord of Kṣmāmūrti.*
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śarva. Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to the fire-form (vahnimūrti).
To the presiding lord of the form of Vahni: *oṃ hāṃ paśupataye namaḥ*. To the form of the Sacrificer (*yajamāna*): *oṃ hāṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttaye namaḥ*.
To the presiding lord of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ ugrāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, salutation to the Sun-form (arkamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the Sun-form—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Rudra.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, salutation to the Water-form (jalamūrti).
To the Lord of the Water-form: *oṃ hāṃ bhavāya namaḥ*.
To the Wind-form: *oṃ hāṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttaye namaḥ*.
To the Lord of the Wind-form: *oṃ hāṃ īśvarāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indumūrti (the Moon-form).
To the Lord of Indumūrti—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Mahādeva.
Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Ākāśamūrti (the Space-form).
To the Lord of the form of space: *oṃ hāṃ bhīmāya namaḥ*.
Having thus worshipped, in the portion of Viṣṇu: *oṃ hrīṃ vidyātatvāya namaḥ*.
To the Lord of the Principle of Knowledge: *oṃ hāṃ viṃ* Viṣṇave *namaḥ*.
Then, the Guru should worship at the side of the image, starting from the east and ending in the northeast, as follows:
*oṃ hāṃ lūṃ* Kṣmāmūrtaye *namaḥ*.
To the Lord of the Earth-form: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śarva.
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to the Fire-form.
To the Lord of the Fire-form: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Paśupati.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the form of the sacrificer (yajamāna-mūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of the sacrificer: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ugra.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the form of Arka.
Salutation to the lord of the form of the Sun.
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two forms of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ yajamānāmūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, salutation to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the Sun-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Rudras.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Water (jalamūrti).
To the two lords of the water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the two Moon-forms (indumūrtti).
To the two Lords of the Moon-forms: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Mahādevas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two Space-forms (ākāśamūrtti).

Having worshipped Śiva in the *liṅga* with the mantra: "Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhīma and Bhīmā," and having performed the *sandhāna*, the Guru, together with the presiding deities (*mūrtipas*), goes to the fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*). Having worshipped Śiva in the fire and offered five oblations (*pañcāhuti*) with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*) for the sake of His presence, the Guru then [proceeds].
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two principles of knowledge (vidyā-tattva) and to the two lords of the principle of knowledge; Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Viṣṇus.
Having thus worshipped in the southeast (Agni),...
Having brought them together, [he should offer] three separate oblations as follows: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ vidyā-tattvābhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two lords of the *vidyā-tattva*: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ viṣṇubhyāṃ svāhā*.
Then, the preceptor situated by the side of the image should perform worship in the southeast.
For example: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Earth (kṣmāmūrtti).
Obeisance to the two lords of the forms of Earth—Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to both Sarva.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrtti).
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.

To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer (*yajamāna*): *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*. To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the Sun-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Rudras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Water (jalamūrti).
To the two lords of the water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Indumūrtis. To the two lords of the Indumūrtis—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Mahādevas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two Ākāśamūrtis.
To the two lords of the form of space: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ,
obeisance to the two Bhīmas.
Having thus worshipped in the fire, one should offer three oblations separately, ending each with *svāhā*.
For example: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrtibhyāṃ svāhā* (to the two forms of Earth);
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śarvābhyāṃ svāhā* (to the two lords of the form of Earth).
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ svāhā to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrti). To the two presiding deities of the forms of Fire—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupatibhyāṃ namaḥ.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ namaḥ to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamāna).
To the two presiding deities of the Sacrificer-form: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ svāhā*.
(L. 4) *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ arkamūrttibhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two presiding deities of the Sun-form: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rudrābhyāṃ svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, svāhā to the two Water-forms (jalamūrti). To the two Lords of the Water-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ, svāhā.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, svāhā to the two Air-forms (vāyumūrti).
To the two lords of the Vāyu-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two Moon-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ indumūrttibhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two lords of the Moon-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ mahādevābhyāṃ svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the two whose forms are space;
[and] to the two lords of the form of space: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the two Bhīmas.
Thus, with three oblations.

Having satisfied [the deities], the Guru should then offer oblations with the root mantra one thousand times, or five hundred, or half of that; having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, he should offer a tenth part for the Brahma-mantras and limbs (*aṅga*), perform the *pūrṇāhuti* again, and according to the availability of materials and time, offer one hundred oblations with the root mantra, perform the *pūrṇāhuti* once more, and after offering for the Brahma-mantras and limbs, perform the final *pūrṇāhuti*. Then, together with the image-makers (*mūrttipas*), the Guru should take the *śāntikumbha* (peace-pitcher), go near the *liṅga*, and sprinkle Śiva with the water from the *śāntikumbha* while reciting the root mantra.

Having touched the portion of Viṣṇu with the middle of the *kuśa* grass, and having recited [the mantra] three times according to the number of oblations (*homa*), it is as follows: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the *kṣmāmūrti*: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śarvābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Paśupatis.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, salutation to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamāna).
To the two lords of the *yajamāna* and *mūrti*: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ arkamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the *arka* and *mūrti*: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rudrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two Water-forms (jalamūrti). [Salutation] to the two Lords of the Water-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ, salutation.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, salutation to the two Air-forms (vāyumūrti).
To the two lords of the Vāyu-mūrti: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Īśvaras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Vidya-tattvas; obeisance to the two lords of the Vidya-tattva.
Then, at the side of the image, the Guru [recites]:
"Sūṃ Sūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Indu."
To the two lords of the Moon-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ mahādevābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two [lords] of the Space-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ ākāśamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*. To the two lords of the Space-forms (*ākāśamūrttyadhipābhyām*): *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhīmābhyāṃ namaḥ*.

Having thus recited [the mantra], the Guru then recites the root-mantra one thousand times, or five hundred, or half of that, or a hundred; having recited it, he then recites a tenth part for the Brahma-aṅgas. Then the Guru, having brought about their presence by means of the Heart [mantra], having rendered them impervious by means of the Armour [mantra], and having restrained them, shall cause Viṣṇu, the Lord of the Tattvas, to hear his command:
"O Viṣṇu, abiding in the plane of the Vidyā-tattva, as long as faults have arisen, so long must you remain right here within this Liṅga through your presence."
Having thus made this request, the Guru,
having worshipped the [moon-]dot with the recitation of "Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to the Vidyā-tattva and Śiva-tattva," should then [proceed].
"Oṃ hrīṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu and Śiva, who are the principles of Vidyā and Śiva.
Having thus worshipped, the Guru then performs the *sandhāna* (unification) at the side of the image:
"Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, obeisance to the Mūrti and Kṣmā."
To the two lords of the earth-form (kṣmāmūrtti): *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ* to Śarva and [Umā], *namaḥ*.
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ* to the two fire-forms (*vahnimūrti*), *namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the fire-form: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ* to Paśupati and [Umā], *namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of the sacrificer,
and to the two presiding deities of the sacrificer’s forms.
— Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Ugras. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the two Arkamūrtis.
To the two lords of the Arkamūrtis: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Rudras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutations to the two Water-forms (jalamūrtti). To the two Lords of the Water-forms: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ, salutations.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ, salutations to the two Wind-forms (vāyumūrtti).
To the two presiding deities of the Vāyu-form: oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Īśvaras;
oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the two Indu-forms.
To the two presiding deities of the Indu-form: oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Mahādevas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two whose forms are space (ākāśamūrtibhyām). [Salutation] to the two lords of the forms of space—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Bhīmas.
Having thus performed the mental union (sandhāna) and worshipped Śiva in the *liṅga*, then the Guru stands by the side of the image (*mūrtti*).

Having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) and worshipped Śiva in the fire, and having offered five oblations with the root mantra for the sake of his presence, the Guru [should then recite]:
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ namaḥ to Śiva and Śivatattva;
oṃ hāṃ hāṃ namaḥ to the two lords of the Śivatattva—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ namaḥ to Śiva and Śivā*.
Having thus worshipped and caused [the deities] to be present, one should offer oblations separately with three offerings for each:
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śivatatvābhyāṃ svāhā* (to the two principles of Śiva); *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śivābhyāṃ svāhā* (to the two Lords of the principle of Śiva).
Having thus offered oblations, the preceptor standing by the side of the image, having worshipped in the fire, [recites]: "Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, salutations to the two forms of Earth (kṣmāmūrti),
and to the two lords of the forms of Earth."
(oṃ hāṃ hāṃ) Homage to both [the hands].
oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ homage to the two forms of fire.
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two forms of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, salutation to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the two lords of the solar forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Rudras.
(L. 3) Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Water (jalamūrti).
To the two lords of the water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ indumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*. (l. 4) To the two lords of the moon-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ mahādevābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are space (ākāśamūrtibhyām).
[Obeisance] to the two lords of the forms of space (ākāśamūrttyadhipābhyām)—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the two Bhīmas.
Having thus worshipped, one should offer three oblations separately with each [mantra] ending in svāhā.
As it is said:
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttibhyāṃ svāhā. To the two lords of the earth-forms—(Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ)—to the two Śarvas, svāhā.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of Fire. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the two lords of the forms of Fire. Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupati-bhyāṃ svāhā.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of the Sacrificer.
To the two presiding deities of the form of the sacrificer: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the two Ugras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the Sun-forms: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the two Rudras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, svāhā to the two forms of Water (jalamūrti).
To the two Lords of the Water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two Wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttibhyāṃ svāhā*.
To the two Lords of the Wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarābhyāṃ svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, svāhā to the two whose forms are the moon;
[svāhā] to the two lords of the moon-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the two Mahādevas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, svāhā to the two whose forms are space.
To the two lords of the forms of space: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Bhīma and Bhīmā.

Having thus offered oblations—then the Guru, having offered one thousand, five hundred, or a hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, having offered a tenth part (*daśāṃśa*) for the Brahma-mantras and their limbs, having offered the *pūrṇāhuti*, and having offered a hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra* according to the availability of materials and time, having offered the [limbs] and performed the *pūrṇāhuti*—thereafter, the Guru, taking the *śānti-kumbha* together with the *mūrtipas*, goes near the *liṅga* and, with the water from the *śānti-kumbha*...

Having sprinkled Śiva with the root mantra using the tip of a *kuśa* blade, and having touched the portion for the *mudrās*, one should recite [the mantra] three times separately according to the number of oblations (*homasaṅkhyā*), as follows:
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, salutation to the two embodiments of the earth (kṣmāmūrti).
To the two lords of the embodiments of the earth—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Śarvas.
(Line 2) Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two principles of Śiva (śivatattva).
To the two Lords of the Śiva-tattva—the two Śivas—salutation.
Then, the preceptor standing by the side of the Mūrti:
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, salutation to Vahni and Mūrti.
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ paśupatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*. To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, salutation to the two Sun-forms (arkamūrti).
To the two lords of the Sun-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Rudras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, salutation to the two Water-forms (jalamūrti).
To the two lords of the water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhavābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ īśvarābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, salutation to the two Moon-forms (indumūrtti).
To the two lords of the Moon-forms—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutation to the two Mahādevas.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two Space-forms (ākāśamūrtti).

With the two lords of the forms of space— *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ bhīmābhyāṃ namaḥ*— having thus recited [this mantra], the Guru then, having recited the root mantra a thousand times, or half of that, or half of that again, and having recited a tenth part for the Brahma-mantras and the limbs (*aṅga*s),

the Guru, having brought them into proximity by means of the heart-mantra, having made them pliant with the armor-mantra, and having restrained them, [should address] the Rudra who is the lord of the principles (*tattva*) with the command.
l.1) He should cause it to be heard: "O,
O Rudraśiva, you who are unawakened!"
"O Lord, since the *liṅga* was requested by you as a fault while it was falling from the principle of Śiva (*śivatattva*), this theft [of the *liṅga*] has occurred to that extent here.

Having thus informed [the deity], the Guru, together with the *mūrtipas*, then went to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) for the purpose of purifying the pedestal (*piṇḍikā*). Then the Guru...

Having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa), "I shall perform the purification of the pedestal (piṇḍikā)," one should divide it into three parts as in the case of the liṅga and perform everything accordingly. The procedure for that is as follows: (having gone to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit)—in the pit: *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the self (ātmatattva)*;
to the presiding deity of the principle of the self—*Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the power of action (kriyāśakti)*.
Having thus performed the worship, and then having offered three oblations:
*oṃ hāṃ ātmatattvāyai svāhā* [to the Mistress of the Principle of Self]; *oṃ hāṃ kriyāśaktyai svāhā* [to the Power of Action].
Afterwards, the preceptor, together with the image-makers, should perform worship in the fire:
*Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti*.
To the presiding deity of Kṣmāmūrti: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā*.
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, salutation to Vahnimūrti. [Salutation] to the presiding deity of Vahnimūrti: Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Dīptamati. Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, salutation to Yajamānamūrti.
To the presiding deity of the Yajamāna-form: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ugrā.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to Arkamūrti. To the presiding deity of the Arkamūrti-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the Water-form (jalamūrti). To the Lord of the Water-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Consciousness (cetanā). Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to the Air-form (vāyumūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of Vāyu (i.18b,
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Balotghaṭā.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indumūrti; to the presiding deity of Indumūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ;
oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Ākāśamūrti. (l. 2)
Having worshipped with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Vibhuvī, the presiding deity of the form of space," one should offer three oblations for each [deity] individually and separately. Then,
the preceptor situated beside the forms [should perform the rite].
Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttyai svāhā.
To the sovereign of the earth-form: Oṃ hrīṃ dhārikāyai svāhā.
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ vahnimūrttyai svāhā.
To the presiding deity of the form of Fire: *oṃ hrīṃ dīptamatyai svāhā*.
To the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttyai svāhā*. To the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hrīṃ ugrāyai svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the Sun-form (arkamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the Sun-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to Jyotsnā.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the two Water-forms (jalamūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the water-form: *oṃ hrīṃ cetanāyai svāhā*.
To the wind-form: *oṃ hāṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttyai*.
To the presiding deity of the wind-form: *oṃ hrīṃ balotghaṭāyai svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, svāhā to Indumūrti; [svāhā] to the presiding deity of Indumūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to Dhatri; oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, svāhā to Ākāśamūrti.
To the lords of the forms of space: *oṃ hrīṃ vibhavyai svāhā*.
Having thus offered the oblation, the Guru [recites]:
*oṃ hrīṃ*.

(i.19a, f.8b, l.1) *Kriyāśaktyai svāhā*. Having offered half a thousand, or half of that, or a hundred oblations; having offered the ten limbs of Brahmā; having offered the full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) according to the requirements of the materials and the time; having offered a hundred oblations with the root mantra; having offered the limbs of Brahmā; and having performed the full oblation—then all the attendants and the Guru standing by the side of the image [should proceed].

Having taken the *śānti*-water jar and gone near the pedestal, the Guru, standing in his respective direction, sprinkles [the area] with the water from the *śānti*-jar while reciting the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).

Then, touching the base of the pedestal with the root of a *kuśa* blade while reciting the mantra "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kriyāśakti," he should mutter it three times separately according to the number of oblations (*homasaṃkhyā*). This is the sequence.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Principle of the Self (ātmatattva). Obeisance to the Sovereign of the Principle of the Self. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Power of Action (kriyāśakti).
Having thus performed the worship, the Guru [should proceed] to the side of the image.
Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti; to the presiding deity of Kṣmāmūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā. Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Vahnimūrti.
To the presiding deity of the form of Fire: Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Dīptamati.
Oṃ Hāṃ Śūṃ, obeisance to the form of the Sacrificer (Yajamānamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer: Oṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Ugrā. (l. 7)
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the Sun-form (arkamūrti). To the presiding deity of the Sun-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the Water-form (jalamūrti).
To the lord of the water-forms— Oṃ Hrīṃ,
salutation to Cetanā.
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to Vāyumūrti.
To the presiding deity of Vāyumūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balotghaṭā.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indumūrti.
To the presiding deity of the lunar form—Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ.
Oṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to the Ākāśa-form.
To the presiding deity of the Ākāśa-form—Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Vibhvī.
Having thus recited [the mantra], the Guru then recites:

*oṃ hrīṃ kriyāśaktyai namaḥ*. Having recited it five hundred times, or half of that, or a hundred times, and having recited the Brahmā-aṅgas, he then sprinkles the Peace-pitchers (*śāntikumbha*) with the *bho* and *bhi* [mantras]. Afterwards, the Guru, having established their presence by means of the Heart-mantra itself, recites: *oṃ haiṃ kavacāyai namaḥ*.
Having enveloped [the disciple] and restrained [his senses], one should cause him to hear the command of the Lord of Reality (*tattvādhipa*):
"O you who have arisen from the defects [of existence], remain right here in this presence for the sake of the power of action (*kriyāśakti*) until the end of the *pīṭha*."
Thus, having worshipped the portion belonging to Brahmā on the pedestal, one should then worship the portion belonging to Viṣṇu. Then the Guru [recites]:
"Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ, salutations to the two principles of the Self (ātmatattva) and Knowledge (vidyātattva)."
With the two presiding deities of the principles of the Self and the principles of Knowledge— *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ kriyājñānibhyāṃ namaḥ*—
having thus meditated upon and worshipped them, the Guru, together with the image-makers (*mūrttipas*), [should worship] with:
*oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the earth-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhārikābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two fire-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ vahnimūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the form of Fire: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dīptamatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two forms of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two presiding deities of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ ugrābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti). To the two presiding deities of the solar form: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two Jyotsnās.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the two forms of Water (jalamūrti).
To the two lords of the water-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ cetanābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two wind-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ yūṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the wind-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ balotghaṭābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, salutation to the two Moon-forms (indumūrti).
To the two lords of the Moon-forms—oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two Dhātrīs.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, salutation to the two Space-forms (ākāśamūrti).

Having joined [the mantras] with "Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two presiding deities of the space-forms (ākāśamūrttyadhipau)," and having worshipped them, then the preceptor standing by the [deity] forms (mūrtipārśvaguru) goes to the vicinity of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa), worships the fire, and, having meditated upon its presence, offers five oblations (āhuti) with the root mantra (mūla). Then the preceptor...
Oṃ hīṃ hīṃ, salutations to the two principles of the Self (*ātmatattva*) and Knowledge (*vidyātattva*).
Salutations to the two presiding deities of the principles of the Self and Knowledge—Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutations to the two [deities] of Action (*kriyā*) and Wisdom (*jñāna*).
Having thus worshipped and offered three oblations, as follows:

Oṃ hīṃ hīṃ, svāhā to the two principles of the Self (ātmatattva) and Knowledge (vidyātattva). Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the two presiding deities of the principles of the Self and Knowledge—the two possessing Action (kriyā) and Knowledge (jñāna). Having thus offered the oblation, then [the Guru...]

(i.20b, l.1) … (oṃ hāṃ hāṃ) yūṃ yūṃ, salutation to the two forms of Wind (vāyumūrtibhyām). To the two lords of the forms of Wind— oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Balotghaṭa and [his consort] (balotghaṭābhyām).
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ sūṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are the Moon (Indumūrti). Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two presiding deities of the forms (Mūrttyadhipa).
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two whose forms are Space (Ākāśamūrti).

Having recited "Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the two lords of the forms of space," the Guru then [recites] "obeisance to [the goddess] ...ti" one thousand times, or five hundred, or fifty, or one hundred; and having recited the mantras of the Brahma-aṅgas and the ten aṅgas, the Guru then [proceeds].
Having brought them into proximity by means of the heart-mantra, having made them firm with the armor-mantra (*varman*), and having restrained them... one should cause them to hear the command:

"O Controller of the principle of Śiva who is known through the power of will (*icchā-śakti*), as long as this seat is required for the sake of [removing] defects, so long may the Goddess remain here. Having thus informed [them], [one should act] like the pedestal; at the time of recitation (*japa*), one should perform [the rite] upon the foundation stone (*ādhāraśilā*) with:
*oṃ sūṃ ādhāraśaktyai namaḥ*. At the time of the fire-oblation (*homa*), one should perform everything [with]: *oṃ sūṃ ādhāraśaktyai svāhā*.

Having likewise approached the vicinity of the *kuṇḍa* for Vṛṣabheśvara, and having performed the rites beginning with the deposition of the *ādhāraśakti*, the offering of oblations (*āhutitarpaṇa*), and so forth—up to the deities of the principles (*tatva*) and their presiding lords (*mūrttīśvara*)—one should offer one hundred oblations together with the final full oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*) while reciting: *oṃ hrīṃ vṛṣabhāya svāhā*. Then, having gone near that [deity], one should perform the sprinkling with the *śāntikumbha* jar, the touching of the roots, middles, and tips of *kuśa* grass, the performance of the recitation (*japa*), and the unification (*sandhāna*) with the Mistress of the Principles (*tatveśvarī*).
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhātryai svāhā | Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ hūṃ hūṃ ākāśamūrttibhyāṃ svāhā | To the two whose form is space— Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ vibhuvyai svāhā |
Having thus offered oblations, the Guru [should offer]: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ icchāśaktyai svāhā*.

Having offered one thousand, half of that, or a hundred oblations, and having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, he should offer ten parts for the limbs of Brahmā, perform the *pūrṇāhuti* again, and [proceed] according to the materials and time...

Having offered one hundred oblations with the *mūla-mantra*, having offered oblations for the limbs of Brahmā, and having performed the *pūrṇāhuti*, the Guru, together with the image-makers (*mūrttipas*), takes the *śānti-kumbha* and goes near the pedestal. Having sprinkled the pedestal with water from the *śānti-kumbha* while reciting the *mūla-mantra*: "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Icchā-śakti," and having touched the portion belonging to Rudra with the tip of a *kuśa* blade, he should mutter [the mantra] as many times as there were oblations, reciting it separately three times, as follows: [in the middle...
(Oṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ Lūṃ Lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmā and Mūrtti).
To the two lords of the earth-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dhārikābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two fire-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ vahnimūrttibhyāṃ namaḥ*. To the two lords of the fire-forms: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ dīptamatibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ śūṃ śūṃ, salutation to the two forms of the Sacrificer (yajamānamūrti).
To the two presiding deities of the Sacrificer’s forms: Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the two Ugras.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ ṣūṃ, salutation to the two forms of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the two lords of the solar form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ jyotsnābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two water-forms: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ pūṃ pūṃ jalamūrtibhyāṃ namaḥ*.
To the two lords of the water-form: *oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ...* (the subsequent folios are missing).

Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ, salutations to the *vidyā-tattva* and the *śiva-tattva*; salutations to Jñāna and Icchā, the presiding deities of the *vidyā-tattva* and the *śiva-tattva*. Then the Guru and the Guru situated beside the *mūrti* [should perform the rite].
(I.21b, f.1a, l.1) And the *śānti-kumbhas*, consecrated a hundred times with the *astra-mantra*, [should be prepared].

Having offered the *sampāta* oblations, one should thereafter worship Śiva properly in the center of the *kuṇḍa*. Having placed the four *kalās* upon the *mekhalās*, the *mūrti* at the *nābhi*, and the *śakti* at the *oṣṭha*, and having established the *āda* with the lip, one should join the channels (*nāḍī*) together—those residing in the jar, on the sacrificial ground, in the fire, and within Śiva and oneself—and then form the channel resembling the fibers of a lotus stalk (*ūrutanu*).
To effect his presence (*sannidhāna*), one should offer three oblations with the root mantra (*mūla-mantra*).
In the *kuṇḍa*: "Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti.
Having thus worshipped and offered three oblations, as follows: (l. 4) "Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Ādhāraśakti."
Having thus offered oblations—with "Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to the principle of the self (ātmatattva);
to the Lord of the principle of the self: Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Brahmā"—and having worshipped in this manner, one should offer three oblations for each [deity].
Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to the principle of the self (ātmatattva).
To the lord of the principle of the self—Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Brahmā.
Having thus offered the oblation, the preceptor, together with the image-makers, [should perform it] in the sacrificial pits starting from the east.
Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti;
to the Lord of Kṣmāmūrti—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śarva;
oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Vahnimūrti.
To the lord of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ paśupataye namaḥ*.
To the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttaye namaḥ*. To the lord of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ ugrāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, homage to the Sun-form (arkamūrti).
To the Lord of the Solar Form: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to Rudra;
*oṃ hāṃ pūṃ* obeisance to the Water Form.
To the Lord of the Water Form: *oṃ hāṃ* obeisance to Bhava.
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, homage to the form of Vāyu.
To the lord of the form of Vāyu—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Īśvara.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, homage to the form of Indu.
To the Lord of the Moon-form: *oṃ hāṃ mahādevāya namaḥ*.
To the Space-form: *oṃ hāṃ hūṃ ākāśamūrttaye namaḥ*. To the Lord of the Space-form: *oṃ hāṃ bhīmāya namaḥ*.
Having thus performed the worship, one should offer three oblations as follows:
*oṃ hāṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttaye svāhā*;
to the Lord of the Earth-form (*kṣmāmūrttyadhipati*): *oṃ hāṃ sarvāya svāhā*.
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, svāhā to the form of Fire (vahnimūrti). To the Lord of the form of Fire—Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Paśupati.
Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, obeisance to the form of the Sacrificer (yajamānamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the Sacrificer’s form: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ugra.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, svāhā to the Sun-form (arka-mūrti).
To the presiding deity of the Sun-form: Oṃ hāṃ, svāhā to Rudra.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, svāhā to the Water-form; to the Lord of the Water-form—oṃ hāṃ bhavāya, svāhā. Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, svāhā to the Wind-form.
To the Lord of the Wind-form: Oṃ hāṃ, to Īśvara, svāhā!
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, to the Moon-form, svāhā!
To the Lord of the Moon-form.
Oṃ hāṃ mahādevāya svāhā.
Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ ākāśamūrttaye svāhā.
To the Lord whose form is space: *oṃ hāṃ bhīmāya svāhā*.

Having thus gratified [the deities] individually with three oblations each, the Guru then offers one thousand, five hundred, or one hundred oblations with the root mantra (*mūla*), performs the *pūrṇāhuti*, and offers a tenth part of the oblations for the Brahma-mantras and the ancillary limbs (*aṅga*). Having performed the *pūrṇāhuti* again, he offers one hundred oblations with the root mantra and the ancillary limbs according to the availability of materials and time, and performs the *pūrṇāhuti* once more. Then, together with the image-makers (*mūrttipa*), the Guru takes the *śāntikumbha* (peace-pitcher) and goes near the *liṅga*.

Having sprinkled Śiva with the water from the *śānti*-vessel using the root mantra and the base of a *kuśa* blade, and having touched the portion belonging to Brahmā, one should recite [the mantra] three times according to the number of oblations, as follows:
*oṃ hāṃ lūṃ kṣmāmūrttaye namaḥ*;
to the Lord of the Earth-form (*kṣmāmūrtti*), *oṃ hāṃ śarvāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, salutation to the fire-form (vahnimūrti). To the lord of the fire-form—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Paśupati. Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, salutation to the sacrificer-form (yajamānamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer (yajamānamūrttyadhipati): Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ugra.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to Arkamūrti.
To the presiding deity of Arkamūrti: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Rudra.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, homage to the Water-form;
[homage] to the Lord of the Water-form.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Principle of the Self (ātmatattva); [homage] to the Lord of the Principle of the Self.
Then, to the side of the form of Brahmā, the Guru [says]:
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Bhava.
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to the form of Vāyu.
To the lord of the form of Vāyu—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśvara.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to the form of Indu.
To the Lord of the Moon-form: Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Mahādeva.
Oṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ, obeisance to the Space-form.
To the Lord of the Space-form: Oṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Bhīma.

Having thus recited [the mantra], the Guru then recites the root-mantra one thousand times, or five hundred, or one hundred; having recited the ten-fold portion for the Brahmā-aṅgas, the Guru, having caused them to become present by means of the heart[-mantra] alone, having [performed] the *varṇanyāsa* and *vamṛṇya*, and having restrained [them], should cause the Lord of the Tattvas to hear the command: "O Brahman, Lord of the Ātma-tattva, as long as this *liṅga* remains raised due to defects, you must remain right here in a state of presence. Having thus informed him, the Guru [recites]:
"Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Ātma-tattva and Vidyā-tattva."
Thus, having worshipped up to Māyā along with the recitation by the learned, and having honored them with:
"Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, salutations to Brahmā and Viṣṇu through the principles of Ātman and Vidyā," then the preceptor stands at the side of the image.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ lūṃ lūṃ, salutations to the two forms of Earth (kṣmāmūrtti).
To the two lords of the forms of Earth—(oṃ hāṃ hāṃ)—salutations to all.
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ rūṃ rūṃ, [salutations] to the two forms of Fire (vahnimūrtti)... [continuation missing]
Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Rudra.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the Water-form.
To the Lord of the Water-form: Oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Bhava.
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, obeisance to the Wind-form. To the Lord of the Wind-form: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Īśvara.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indumūrti;
to the lord of Indumūrti—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Mahādeva;
oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Ākāśamūrti.
To the Lord of the Space-form: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Sadāśiva*.
Having thus worshipped, the Guru [worships] in the Brahma-sector: *Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Ātma-tattva*.
To the Lord of the Principle of the Self (ātmatattva)— *oṃ hāṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ*.
Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), the Guru standing by the side of the image then [proceeds] by skipping the preceding [deities].
Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti. Obeisance to the Lord of Kṣmāmūrti—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śarva. Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Vahnimūrti.
To the Lord of the form of Fire: *oṃ hāṃ paśupataye namaḥ*.
To the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttaye namaḥ*. To the Lord of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ ugrāya namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, homage to the Sun-form (arkamūrti).
To the Lord of the Sun-form: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Rudra.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, homage to the Water-form (jalamūrti).
To the Lord of the Water-form: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Bhava.
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, salutation to the Wind-form. To the Lord of the Wind-form.
(om hāṃ) Homage to Īśvara.
om hāṃ sūṃ homage to Indumūrti.
To the Lord of the Moon-form: Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Mahādeva.
Oṃ Hāṃ Hūṃ, salutation to the Space-form.
To the Lord of the Space-form: Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Bhīma.
Having thus assigned the embodied and the lords of the embodiments to each sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should restrain [them].
According to the teacher’s instruction, one should slowly recite the mantra beginning with *agnāde*.
Consisting of the power of resonance (*nāda-śakti*), subtle, and non-dispersing due to its integration (*sandhāna*).

By means of the yoga of not abandoning the causal [state], [the breath] has emerged from the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), possessing the luster of a thousand suns and equal to ten million lightning bolts.
With a canopy of shimmering rays, it pervades the earth and the space between the quarters; and having mentally dissolved the mantra, it attains the outpouring of the essence of bliss.
Having brought down from the "End of the Twelve" (*dvādaśānta*) the partless, all-pervading Śiva—
Endowed with thirty-eight marks and blazing with a thousand rays.
Having meditated upon [the deity] as consisting of all powers, complete with limbs, resembling a garland of light,
and bearing a radiant orb upon the forehead, he brought it to the door of the uvula.
Having meditated on [the breath] as it has emerged through the *suṣumnā*, vibrating and moving like a serpent,
one should deposit it, pervading everything, through the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
O God, the placement of the soul (jīva-nyāsa) in the liṅga accomplishes all goals;
it consists of installation (sthāpana), invocation (sannidhāna), binding (sannirodhana), and piercing (avakuṇṭhana).

l.1) Having consecrated the hand-gestures (*mudrā*) with water for showing, water for washing the feet, water for sipping, and water for welcoming (*arghya*), along with flowers, and having worshipped them, one should likewise cover them with a cloth.
Alternatively, one should provide three outer enclosures made of ashes, darbha grass, and sesame seeds.
Then, beginning from the stalk at the base of the pedestal, the Guru [should offer]:
"Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Śakti-tattva; obeisance to the Sovereign of the Śakti-tattva;
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Śaktimān."
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Śiva-tattva. To the Lord of the Śiva-tattva—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva. At the crown of the head—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Lord of the Śakti-tattva.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Śakti. At the throat: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Sadāśiva (sadāśivatattva).
To the lord of the principle of Sadāśiva: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of Īśvara.
To the Lord of the principle of Īśvara—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ananta.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of Śuddhavidyā.
To the Lord of the principle of Pure Knowledge (śuddhavidyā-tattva): Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śambara.
On the left side: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Māyā (māyā-tattva). To the Lord of the principle of Māyā: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Gahaneśa.
On the right side—in the region of Viṣṇu—on the chest: *oṃ hāṃ* homage to the principle (*tattva*) of Kalā.
To the lord of the principle of Kalā: *oṃ hāṃ* homage to Kālanātha.
*oṃ hāṃ* homage to the principle of Niyati.
To the Lord of the Principle of Necessity: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Body of Restriction.
Oṃ hāṃ, to the Principle of Limited Agency.
Homage!
To the Lord of the Kalā-tattva—Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to Jñānabindu.
Oṃ Hāṃ, homage to the Vidyā-tattva.
To the Lord of the Principle of Knowledge: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vedavijñāna. (L. 2) Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Principle of Passion. To the Lord of the Principle of Passion: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Kāmadā.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the Puruṣa.
To the Lord of the principle of the Puruṣa—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the subtle body. In the belly—(Oṃ hāṃ) obeisance to the principle of Prakṛti.
To the Lord of the Principle of Primordial Nature: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Pradhānakāya.
On the back: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Guṇatattva.
To the Lord of the Principle of the Qualities: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Trideha.
In the center of the navel: *oṃ hāṃṃ namo buddhitattvāya*. To the lord of the principle of intellect (*buddhitattva*): *oṃ hāṃ namo buddhāya*.
At the three joints: *oṃ hāṃ namo ’haṃkāratattvāya*.
To the Lord of the principle of ego (*ahaṃkāra-tattva*): *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to the one who has become ego (*ahaṃkṛtatvaye namaḥ*).
In the Brahma-quarter: salutation to the principle of mind (*manas-tattvāya namaḥ*). To the Lord of the principle of mind: *oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to volition (*saṅkalpāya namaḥ*).
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of the hearer (*śrotṛtattva*).
To the lord of the principle of the hearer—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the sky-walker (*vyomacārin*).
In the skin—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the skin (*tvaktattva*).
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Lord of the principle of skin—(oṃ hāṃ)—to all the limbs.
In the eyes: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of the eye.
To the Lord of the principle of the eye: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Illuminator.
Tongue—
l.1) Homage to the reality of the tongue.
To the Lord of the reality of the tongue: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mahāvaktra. In the nose: Oṃ hāṃ, [homage to the reality of the nose].
To the Lord of the reality of the nose: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vilambaka. (l. 2)
In the mouth: *oṃ hāṃ* homage to the principle of speech (*vāktattva*).
To the lord of the principle of speech: *oṃ hāṃ* homage to Vibhu. *Oṃ hāṃ* homage to the principle of the feet (*pādatattva*).

To the Lord of the reality of the feet: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ramaṇeśa. To the hands: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the reality of the hands. To the Lord of the reality of the hands: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sāmagā.
In the anus: *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the element of the anus (*pāyutatva*). To the lord of the element of the anus: *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to Kuṇṭhakṛt.
In the generative organ: *Oṃ hāṃ*, obeisance to the element of the generative organ (*upasthatatva*).
To the Lord of the *upastha-tattva*: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ghanānanda.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the *śabda-tattva*. To the Lord of the *śabda-tattva*: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣmanāda.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of touch (*sparśa-tattva*).
To the lord of the principle of touch—(Oṃ hāṃ) homage to Balavaktra.
(Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the principle of form (*rūpa-tattva*).
To the Lord of the element of form: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Bhānumat. (Oṃ hāṃ) Homage to the element of taste. To the Lord of the element of taste: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Jalada.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the reality of fragrance (gandha-tattva).
To the lord of the reality of fragrance—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the limb of fragrance (gandhāṅga).
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the reality of space (ākāśa-tattva).
To the Lord of the element of space: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣma.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the element of wind.
To the Lord of the element of air: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mātariśvan.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the element of fire.
To the Lord of the element of fire: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Tviṣṭānideva.
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the water element (jala-tattva).
Salutation to the lord of the water element—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Lord of Waters (jaleśa).
From below the knees to the feet—oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the earth element (pṛthivī-tattva).
To the Lord of the Earth Principle: *Oṃ haṃ śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ*.

Having thus worshipped the Sovereign of the Principles, and having offered a flower garland and a protective cord for the purpose of beholding the three sections (*trikhaṇḍa*), the Guru [worships] in the region of the serpent:
*Oṃ hūṃ śivatattvāyai namaḥ*.

Having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) with "Obeisance to Icchā, the sovereign of the Śiva-tattva," the Guru, together with the presiding deities of the forms (mūrtipas), [proceeds] from the east to the end of the directions: "Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti."
To the lord of the earth-form: *oṃ hrīṃ dhārikāyai namaḥ*.
To the fire-form: *oṃ hāṃ rūṃ vahnimūrttyai namaḥ*. To the lord of the fire-form: *oṃ hrīṃ dīptamatyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ śūṃ, homage to the form of the sacrificer (yajamānamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of the sacrificer—oṃ hāṃ hāṃ, homage to Ugrā.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, homage to the form of the Sun (arkamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the solar form—Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Jyotsnā (the Moonlight).
Oṃ Hāṃ Pūṃ, salutation to the Water Form.
To the presiding deity of the water form—Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Cetanā (Consciousness).
Homage!
Oṃ hāṃ yūṃ, homage to the wind-form (vāyumūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of Vāyu: Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Balotghaṭā.
Oṃ Hāṃ Sūṃ, salutation to Indumūrti. To the presiding deity of the form of Indu (the Moon): Oṃ Hrīṃ, salutation to Dhātrī.
Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the one whose form is space (ākāśamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of space—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vibhū (the Pervasive One).
Having thus recited this and performed worship, the Guru [should place it] in the upper portion of the neck of the pedestal, up to the end of the principle of Sadāśiva (sadāśivatattva).
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vidyātattvā; to the Sovereign of the Vidyātattva—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jñānī. Then the Guru, together with the image-makers (mūrttipas), [performs the rite].
