In the east and other directions: Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti.
To the presiding deity of Kṣmāmūrti: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā. Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Vahnimūrti.
To the presiding deity of the form of Fire: Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Dīptamati.
Oṃ Hāṃ Śūṃ, obeisance to the form of the Sacrificer (Yajamānamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer: Oṃ Hāṃ Hāṃ, obeisance to Ugrā.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to Arkamūrti;
to the presiding deity of Arkamūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā;
oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to Jalamūrti.
To the Lord of the Water-form: Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Cetanā.
Oṃ Hāṃ Yūṃ, obeisance to the Wind-form (Vāyumūrti).
To the Lord of the Wind-form: Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Balotghaṭā.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, salutation to Indumūrti;
to the presiding deity of Indumūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Dhātṛ.
Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, salutation to Ākāśamūrti;
to the presiding deity of Ākāśamūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Vibhū.

Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*) and worship, one should then perform the placement up to the end of *māyā*, starting from the base portion of the seat (*pīṭha*) and extending to the region of the throat.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of the self (ātmatattva).
To the presiding deity of the principle of the self—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the power of action (kriyāśakti).
Having thus worshipped, [proceed] from the east and so forth.
Oṃ hāṃ lūṃ, obeisance to Kṣmāmūrti. Obeisance to the Lord of Kṣmāmūrti. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhārikā. Oṃ hāṃ rūṃ, obeisance to Vahnimūrti.
To the presiding deity of the form of Fire: *oṃ hrīṃ dīptamatyai namaḥ*.
To the form of the Sacrificer (*yajamāna*): *oṃ hāṃ śūṃ yajamānamūrttyai namaḥ*. To the presiding deity of the form of the Sacrificer: *oṃ hāṃ hāṃ ugrāyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ ṣūṃ, obeisance to the Sun-form (arkamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the Sun-form: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā.
Oṃ hāṃ pūṃ, obeisance to the Water-form (jalamūrti).
To the presiding deity of the water-form: *oṃ hrīṃ cetanāyai namaḥ*.
To the wind-form: *oṃ hāṃ yūṃ vāyumūrttyai namaḥ*.
To the presiding deity of the wind-form: *oṃ hrīṃ balotghaṭāyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ hāṃ sūṃ, obeisance to Indumūrti;
to the presiding deity of Indumūrti—oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Dhātṛ.
Oṃ hāṃ hūṃ, obeisance to Ākāśamūrti. (l. 7)

Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vibhuvī, the sovereign of the form of space," and having restrained [the breath], one should perform the placement with "Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kriyāśakti."
Alternatively— having uttered the mantra ending with the Śakti, namely: *oṃ hrīṃ saḥ mahāgaurīrudradayite svāhā* (I.27b, f.7a, l.1), one should invoke [the deity], install her, and then dissolve her.
Having thus placed [the deity] upon the bull— *oṃ hrīṃ vṛṣabhāya namaḥ*—
and having invoked him, one should restrain [him]; then, having also placed the god upon the foundational stone (*ādhāraśilā*)— *oṃ sūṃ ādhāraśaktyai namaḥ*.

Having invoked [the deities] with "oṃ hrīṃ vāṃ," one should meditate on three external enclosures made of ash, *darbha* grass, and sesame seeds for these [deities]. Thus, in the consecration of the practitioner (*sādhaka*), one should install the forms (*mūrti*) and the lords of the forms (*mūrtīśvara*), as well as the eight Lords of Knowledge (*vidyeśvara*). In the consecration of the lords of the forms, one should worship the forms beginning with Nivṛtti and the lords of the forms beginning with Sadyojāta, starting from the west and ending in the east, according to the previously prescribed rule. Having cooked the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) and offered it at each fire-pit (*kuṇḍa*), one should perform the oblations using the peace-vases (*śāntikumbha*), which have been consecrated a hundred times with the Weapon-mantra (*astra-mantra*) and [properly] prepared.
l.1) *Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the seat of Gaurī.* Having thus worshipped the seat and placed a handful of flowers at the region of the heart: *Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Gaurī.*
Thus, having recited up to the *dvādaśānta* and performed worship according to the visualization:
*oṃ hrīṃ gaurīyai namaḥ*. *oṃ hrīṃ īśānamūrthāyai namaḥ*.
Oṃ seṃ, obeisance to the face of Tatpuruṣa.
Oṃ suṃ, obeisance to the heart of Aghora.
Oṃ sīṃ, obeisance to the secret organ of Vāmadeva.

Oṃ saṃ, obeisance to the form of Sadyojāta. (l. 3) Having thus performed the placement on the portion of the staff, one should perform the placement on the portion of the kalās as well: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the nivṛtti-kalā.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the kalā of Pratiṣṭhā. Oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the kalā of Vidyā. Oṃ hraiṃ, obeisance to the kalā of Śānti.
"Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the digit Śāntyatītakalā.
Having thus performed the placement of the digits (*kalānyāsa*), and having worshipped the limbs, sub-limbs, joints, minor limbs, and major limbs, [one places]:
"Oṃ hrīṃ ṭhaṃ" on the head. (l. 5)
Oṃ śrīṃ paṃ on the face;
oṃ śrīṃ ṭaṃ on the forehead;
oṃ śrīṃ ḍaṃ on the right cheek.
Oṃ śrīṃ ḍhaṃ on the left cheek;
Oṃ śrīṃ naṃ on the nose;
Oṃ śrīṃ baṃ on the right ear. (l. 6)
Oṃ śrīṃ bhaṃ in the left ear;
oṃ śrīṃ phaṃ in the right eye;
oṃ śrīṃ maṃ in the left eye.
Oṃ śrīṃ ñaṃ at the chin; oṃ śrīṃ ṇaṃ at the teeth;
oṃ śrīṃ jaṃ at the tongue.
Oṃ śrīṃ kaṃ on the throat;
Oṃ śrīṃ gaṃ at the heart;
Oṃ śrīṃ saṃ on the right arm.
Oṃ śrīṃ ṣaṃ on the left arm; oṃ śrīṃ gaṃ in the belly; oṃ śrīṃ raṃ in the private parts.
Oṃ śrīṃ yaṃ on the right thigh; oṃ śrīṃ vaṃ on the left thigh;
oṃ śrīṃ dhaṃ on the anus.
Oṃ śrīṃ jaṃ on the right knee;
Oṃ śrīṃ laṃ on the left knee;
Oṃ śrīṃ ṅaṃ on the right foot.
Oṃ śrīṃ saṃ on the left foot;
oṃ śrīṃ vaṃ on the ear.
Oṃ śrīṃ śaṃ in the aperture;
thus one should place [the mantra] with the thumb and forefinger joined.
Having thus performed the placement of the limbs—
Oṃ hrīṃ caṃ on the head; oṃ hrīṃ paṃ on the face; oṃ hrīṃ ṣaṃ on the ears.
Oṃ hrīṃ caṃ on the thighs; oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ on the right arm; oṃ śrīṃ (hrīṃ) maṃ on the left arm.
Oṃ hrīṃ raṃ in the belly; oṃ hrīṃ laṃ at the navel; oṃ hrīṃ phaṃ in the private parts.
Oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ at the waist; oṃ hrīṃ baṃ on the back; oṃ hrīṃ huṃ on the right shank.
Oṃ hrīṃ ūṃ on the left calf;
oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ on the right foot;
oṃ hrīṃ ṝṃ on the left foot.
Oṃ hrīṃ yaṃ at the end of the forehead on the right side;
Oṃ hrīṃ bhaṃ between the eyebrows—
thus one should perform the placement using the thumb and middle finger.
Having thus performed the placement upon each limb: Oṃ hrīṃ ṭaṃ on the feet;
Oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ on the waist.
Oṃ hrīṃ yaṃ at the secret place; oṃ hrīṃ uṃ at the navel; oṃ hrīṃ ūṃ at the belly.
Oṃ hrīṃ aṃ on the thighs;
oṃ hrīṃ āṃ in the heart;
oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ in the throat.
Oṃ hrīṃ lṛ on the right hand;
oṃ hrīṃ lṝṃ on the left hand;
oṃ hrīṃ jaṃ on the western part.
Oṃ hrīṃ ṛṃ at the upper part of the western side. Oṃ hrīṃ śaṃ at the chin. Oṃ hrīṃ paṃ at the teeth.
Oṃ hrīṃ maṃ on the tongue; oṃ hrīṃ phaṃ on the nose; oṃ hrīṃ raṃ on the right eye.
Oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ on the left eye; oṃ hrīṃ saṃ on the right ear; oṃ hrīṃ kṣaṃ on the left ear.
Oṃ hrīṃ taṃ on the forehead;
Oṃ hrīṃ ḷaṃ on the head. Thus one should perform the placement using the thumb and ring finger.
Having thus performed the placement of the limbs of enjoyment (*bhogāṅga*), [one recites]:
*oṃ hrāṃ*.
*Oṃ hrīṃ īśānāyai namaḥ*—at the aperture of the crown of the head.
*Oṃ hrīṃ hreṃ tatpuruṣāyai namaḥ*—on the face.
*Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ aghorāyai namaḥ*—on the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ—at the secret place.
Oṃ hrīṃ sadyojātāyai namaḥ—at the feet. Oṃ hrīṃ hrāṃ hṛdayāyai namaḥ—at the right hands.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the head—at the left elbow.
Oṃ hrīṃ hū, obeisance to the crest-lock—at the abdomen. Oṃ hrīṃ hraiṃ, obeisance to the armor—at the nose.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to the eyes—at the two eyes. Oṃ hrīṃ hṛḥ, obeisance to the weapon—at all the limbs.
Oṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī—at the ears.
Oṃ hrīḥ mahālakṣmyai namaḥ—on the forehead.
Oṃ hrīṃ devyai namaḥ—thus, on the cavity of the mouth; one should place [the mantra] on the thumb and little finger.
Having thus worshipped the limbs of dissolution (layāṅga), one should install the internal Mātṛkā below, as follows:
In the Mūlādhāra, on the lower four-petaled platform: *oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ namaḥ*.
In its own station, on the six-petaled [lotus] below: *oṃ hrīṃ vaṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ namaḥ*.
In the Maṇipūra at the throat, on the ten-petaled [lotus]: *oṃ hrīṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ namaḥ*.
Above, in the twelve petals of the *anāhata* [cakra]: *oṃ hrīṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ namaḥ*.
On the upper band, in the sixteen petals of the *viśuddha* [cakra] (l. 8): *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ lṛṃ lṝṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ namaḥ*.
In the portion of Rudra, in the two petals of the *ājñā* [cakra]: *oṃ hrīṃ ḷaṃ kṣaṃ namaḥ*.
At the beginning: Oṃ hrīṃ haṃ namaḥ. (i.30a, f.21b, l.1) Thus ends the internal nyāsa of the Mātṛkās.
Then, having performed the Gaurī-kalā-nyāsa as previously described.
Oṃ hrīṃ tārāyai namaḥ—on the head.
Oṃ hrīṃ vidyāyai namaḥ—on the face. Oṃ hrīṃ muninyai namaḥ—on the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ śuddhāyai namaḥ—at the throat.
Oṃ hrīṃ jarāyai namaḥ—at the left arm.
Oṃ hrīṃ methāyai namaḥ—at the right arm.
Oṃ hrīṃ svadhāmnai namaḥ—in the belly;
oṃ hrīṃ svatyai namaḥ—in the navel;
oṃ hrīṃ varmaṇyai namaḥ—in the genitals.
Oṃ hrīṃ pālinyai namaḥ—at the secret place. Oṃ hrīṃ jvalinyai namaḥ—at the left thigh. Oṃ hrīṃ tṛṣṇāyai namaḥ—at the right thigh. (l. 4)
Oṃ hrīṃ sṛtyai namaḥ — on the left knee.
Oṃ hrīṃ kāmāyai namaḥ — on the right knee.
Oṃ hrīṃ unmanyai namaḥ — on the left shoulder.
Oṃ hrīṃ prajāyai namaḥ—on the right calf.
Oṃ hrīṃ cintyāyai namaḥ—on the left back. Oṃ hrīṃ dhṛtyai namaḥ—on the right back.
Oṃ hrīṃ kriyāyai namaḥ—on the left side.
Oṃ hrīṃ kṣāntyai namaḥ—on the right side.
Oṃ hrīṃ śāntyai namaḥ—on the left foot.
Oṃ hrīṃ dāntyai namaḥ—on the right foot.
Oṃ hrīṃ dayāyai namaḥ—on the left hand. Oṃ hrīṃ svastyai namaḥ.
On the right breast: *oṃ hrīṃ duttyai namaḥ*. On the left breast:
*oṃ hrīṃ saṃnyāyai namaḥ*. On the right breast: [as before]. Having thus performed the Gaurī-kalā-nyāsa.
The *śrīkaṇṭhanyāsa* is as follows:
*oṃ hrīṃ aṃ* *nivṛttyai* *namaḥ*—at the end of the breasts;
*oṃ hrīṃ āṃ* *pratiṣṭhāyai* *namaḥ*—on the forehead.
Oṃ hrīṃ vidyāyai namaḥ—on the right eye. Oṃ hrīṃ īśānyai namaḥ—on the left eye.
Oṃ uṃ guṇḍikāyai namaḥ—on the right ear.

Having offered the *arghya* for cessation with "Oṃ Hrīṃ Ūṃ... [and having completed the preceding rites], one should address the Great Goddess at the conclusion of the welcome: "O Great Goddess! Having visualized that the Goddess has replied, "Welcome, my child," one should perform the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).

Having offered water for the feet and other honors while the Goddess is being established during the time of installation, one should announce: "May there be presence in the *vardhanī* vessel through the state of mutual affection. Then, having offered the welcoming *arghya*, and having performed the placement of the limbs beginning with the heart—*oṃ hrīṃ hṛdayāyai namaḥ*;
*oṃ hrīṃ śirase svāhā*.
Oṃ hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ hraiṃ, huṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Oṃ hauṃ, vaṣaṭ to the eyes (netra).
Oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ. Having thus performed the placement (vinyāsa), [one recites]: Oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ gaurīyai namaḥ.
Having thus contemplated their unity, protected them with the Astra-mantra, enveloped them with the Kavaca-mantra, and offered the Amṛta-mudrā,
one should effect the supreme transformation (*paramīkaraṇa*) by means of the Mahāmudrā, reciting: *oṃ hāṃ hrīṃ mahāgaurīyai namaḥ*.

Having offered water for the feet, water for sipping, and the arghya offering— reciting "oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ mahāgaurīyai namaḥ"— and having rendered [the deity] supreme by means of the great mudrā (mahāmudrā),...
Having offered water for the feet (*pādya*), water for sipping (*ācamana*), and the respectful offering (*arghya*)—
reciting "oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ mahāgaurīyai namaḥ"—

and having presented flowers, *dūrvā* grass, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth with the root mantra, one should hold the incense and lamp in the left hand while ringing the bell before the eyes [of the deity].

As before, having offered water for sipping (ācamana) and the respectful offering (arghya), and having bathed [the deity] with a drop of the arghya water, one should mentally offer various garments with devotion, adorn [the deity] with sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, saffron, mixed perfumes, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), ornaments, and so forth, and [recite]: "Oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ, to the mistress of the principle of the self (ātmatattva)."
Salutation to Gaurī.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ, salutation to Gaurī, the sovereign of the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva).

Having worshipped with "Oṃ hrāṃ hrauṃ, obeisance to Gaurī, the sovereign of the Śiva-tattva," and having adorned her with garlands of flowers and other offerings starting with incense, one should ring the bell with the Astra-mantra,
offer incense, a lamp, water for sipping (ācamana), and the arghya offering, and then display the Manoratha-mudrā.
Then, having worshipped with the mantras of the powers of the five Brahmans and the six limbs at the locations of the dissolution-limbs (layāṅga):
oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ ambikāyai namaḥ | oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ gaṇāmbikāyai namaḥ |
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Gaurī. Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Umā.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Heart, the Śiva-śakti. Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Head, the Ānanda (Ananta)-śakti. Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the Tuft (Śikhā), the Maheśa-śakti.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the armor [tattva] and the Raudra-śakti.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the three eyes and the Sārī-śakti.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the weapon [tattva] and the Sureśa-śakti.

Having thus performed the worship, and having worshipped Gaurī in the center with the root mantra for the sake of the worship of the enclosures (*āvaraṇapūjā*), one should then worship the powers of the eight Lords of Knowledge (*aṣṭavidyeśvara-śakti*) preceded by meditation— from the east to the northeast— with: *oṃ hrīṃ vāmāsanāyai namaḥ* | *oṃ hrīṃ vāmamūrttaye namaḥ* |
The wise practitioner should meditate upon the goddess Vāmā, who has a blue luster, is adorned with a crown and other ornaments, and holds a conch and a discus.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vāmā. Having thus performed the invocation and other rites, and having worshipped her, [one offers:
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jeṣṭhāsanā.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jeṣṭhāmūrtti. Likewise,
[one should meditate on] Jeṣṭhā, who is yellow in color, holds a lotus, and has eyes like a lotus.
Adorned with all ornaments, she was well-proportioned and in the full bloom of youth.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā.
Having thus performed the invocation and other rites, one should worship her with: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of Raudrī.

Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the Fierce Form (Raudramūrti). And the Fierce One has the luster of white and blue; she is three-eyed, holds a trident, wears blue garments, and is adorned with a crown and other ornaments.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Raudrī. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kālyāsanā. Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kālīmūrti.

The wise practitioner should visualize her as being well-proportioned, with a beautiful face and a slight smile, possessing shapely hips and a slender waist, draped in fine silk garments, and adorned with all ornaments.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kālī. Having thus performed the worship beginning with the invocation, [one offers]: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the seat of Kalavikaraṇī.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kalavikaraṇīmūrti. The goddess has the luster of a red lotus, holds a noose in her hand, possesses great strength, wears yellow garments, and carries a *khaṭvāṅga* and a shield.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Kalavikaraṇī. Having thus worshipped her: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balavikartī; Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the form of Balavivikaraṇī.
[One should meditate on] the Goddess who has four arms and three eyes, with tawny hair of a yakṣa rising upwards, possessing the luster of an eye, and holding a noose in her left hand.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balavikaraṇī.
Having thus worshipped her, [one should worship]: Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balapramathanāsanā;
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Balapramathanimūrti.
The goddess Balapramathanī, possessing a splendor equal to the color of blue, bearing a staff,
and of great form.
Adorned with a crown and other ornaments.
Having worshipped with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Balapramadhinī," [one should then worship] with "Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Sarvabhūtadamanyāsana."

Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to the form of Sarvabhūtadamanī. She who subdues all spirits, possessing a complexion like molten gold, in the full bloom of youth, holding a spear in her hand, endowed with great heroism, and adorned with a crown and other ornaments.
"Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to the subduer of all spirits.
Having thus worshipped,
and having offered incense, lamps, food offerings, water for drinking, and betel leaf;
Having worshipped the first and the last [deities], likewise, in the northeast (īśāna),

for the region of Īśāna, who is crystal-colored, whose hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, whose form is as previously described, and who possesses the quality of tranquility: *oṃ hrīṃ umāyai namaḥ*.
To the eastern region, to that which is eastern, yellow-colored, holding a serpent-noose in hand, of immortal form, possessing fierce qualities—
*oṃ hrīṃ gaurīyai namaḥ*. To the southern region, of non-terrible form, deep-blue colored, bearing a bow, most terrifying.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Gaṅgā.
To the northern region, to Vāmadeva, who has a red-colored auspicious seat, who holds a noose and a goad in his hands, and who possesses a gentle form—
oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Ambikā.
To the western direction, to Sadyojāta, who is white in color, steadfast, holding a trident and a skull-cup in his hands, and possessing a fierce form— oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Gaṇāmbikā.
To the southeastern direction, to him whose form is knowledge, the three-eyed one, with hands granting boons and fearlessness—
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Vāminī. To the southeast, to the head, to the yellow-colored one, to the three-eyed one who holds a trident and a skull-cup in his hands—
oṃ hrīṃ, homage to Nīlinī.
One should meditate upon Khaṭvāṅga-khetaka, situated in the southern direction, for the sake of the region of Nirṛti.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Vargā.
I meditate upon her who has the pale-white complexion of the letter-group (varga), who is mounted upon a river, who stands upon a bull, and who is adorned with fierce fangs and a bell in her hand.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Kālakaṇṭhī, who has a white luster and is endowed with a sugarcane bow.
One should meditate on Kālakaṇṭhī as having ascended [to the state of] existence in the western direction.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Nirmmāṇī. I bow to the Goddess Nirmmāṇī, who has the luster of saffron, who is mounted upon a deer,
who possesses ten thousand locks of hair, and who is being meditated upon.
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Nāriṇī.
One should meditate upon Nāriṇī, mounted upon a lion, radiant with ornaments of gold,
holding a flower-arrow, and adorned with various fragrances.
Oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Susukeṭinī!
She is white in color, possesses great strength, and is mounted upon a white-bodied vehicle;
she is endowed with a trident and the gesture of fearlessness, and clearly manifests [the state of] *susu* (deep sleep).
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī.
One should worship Sarasvatī, who is mounted upon a swan, whose limbs are beautiful, who holds a lotus in her hand, and who is pure and endowed with the Vedas. (Verse 7)
Oṃ hrīṃ, salutations to Mahālakṣmī!
I bow to her who bestows auspiciousness, who is seated upon a lotus, who holds a lotus in her hand, who is adorned with a crown and diadem, and who has Vāsuki as her vehicle.
Thus,
having performed the worship, and having worshipped the five enclosures, [one should meditate upon] the two-eyed, three-eyed one in human form, endowed with a dark-blue radiance.
His head was adorned with a skull-ornament, he bore earrings, and his eyes were cruel and fierce.
He holds a sword, a shield, and a skull in the form of a human being; he is black in color, possesses an even radiance, is endowed with all ornaments, and is beautified by every kind of decoration.
With a skull-bowl in his hand... (l.3) he has one face and two eyes, holds a bell, and is white in appearance;
he has two arms and two feet, and is adorned with all ornaments.
Ghaṇṭāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ. Nārāca is of human form, dark green in color, with one face, two eyes, two feet, and is seated upon a lotus.
Nārācāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ.
[One should visualize] the Ḍamaru, black in color, with one face...
[and] endowed with a great mouth, adorned with all ornaments.
To the ḍamaru, huṃ phaṭ, obeisance!
I take refuge in the great-armed one, who has a yellowish luster and a human form, pervading [the universe],
with a banner atop his left side, accompanied by a flag.
To the Banner, *huṃ phaṭ*, obeisance!
[He is] a corpse (*petālaṃ*) in human form, equipped with a sword and a shield,
possessing fierce fangs, white in color, and endowed with great strength.
To the Vetāla, *huṃ phaṭ*! Homage!
And [to] the Razor [and] the One of Fierce Form...
And with two eyes;
when joined with two... it shall bring about the destruction of all enemies.
Kṣurikāya hūṃ phaṭ namaḥ. [The syllable] bhuj is at the navel; above that is pa... (l. 2)... and the oblation (huti) is in the south of the ray (raśmi).

One should bind the person with the vajra-noose. Having satisfied [the deity] with offerings such as *naivedya* according to the instructions of Nairṛta, and having performed the recitation (*japa*), one should present the water for the *arghya* offering into the hand of the Goddess, who has arisen from the *utthāna* [mudrā].

(i.34b, f.29a, l.1) To Śiva preceded by the form of Maheśvara, [and] Ānana and the others; to the Śivatattva; to Āditya, Vasiṣṭha, Atri, Viśva, Sādhya, Marut, Bhṛgu, and Aṅgāra; thereafter, to the three [sages] with the sacred thread around the neck, obeisance to ... Pulastya, Kṛta...

Bhāradvāja, Viśvāmitra, Pracetas, Ṛcchaka, Abhiṣṭya, Dadhīśa, Pūrva 11, Sākā 10, Vauṣaṭ to Sanātana, Sāstā, Sanātanā, Sanatkumāra, Kapila, Pañcaśis, and Vṛṣabha—thus for the seventh year. Vauṣaṭ to all beings. Salutations to Kāśyapa. To Vāyu, Naidhruva, Dakṣiṇahasta, Dopa, Vatikavya, Vāhana, Vasu, Anila, Soma, Yama, Madhuka, Varhi, and Ājipa.

[The mantra] beginning with "ati devīpavitra... [is offered] to Īśāna, the Father, Śadāśiva, and Śānta; thus [it is for] the specific ancestors, to all the grandfathers, to all the great-grandfathers, to all those who are favorable, to the white water, to the piercer, to the Guru, to the Preceptor, to the ash, to the intellect, and to the primordial source. (I.35a, f.29b, l.1)

Then, having sipped water, performed the ritual of the limbs (*sakalīkaraṇa*), and completed the internal sacrifice and the internal meditation within the heart, he made this request: "I shall worship externally"— *oṃ hauṃ*, obeisance to the *kalā* beyond peace (*śāntyatīta*), on the head.
Oṃ haiṃ, homage to Śāntikalā—on the face.
Oṃ hūṃ, homage to Vidyākalā—on the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Pratiṣṭhākalā—on the navel.
Oṃ hlāṃ, salutation to Nivṛttikalā—at the feet.
Having thus performed the placement (vinyāsa):
Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Tirodhānaśakti—above the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
At the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Śiva-tattva.
To the Lord of the Śiva-tattva: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Śiva.
On the head (mūrdhan): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Śakti-tattva.
To the Lord of the Śakti-tattva: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śaktimān.
From the top of the head down to the lower part, and above the *bandī* (the hairline), on the forehead: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the Sadāśiva-tattva.
To the Lord of the Sadāśiva-tattva: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Brahmā.
At the throat: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Īśvara (Īśvaratattva).
To the lord of the principle of Īśvara: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ananta. Below the throat: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of Pure Knowledge (Śuddhavidyātattva).
To the Lord of the principle of Pure Knowledge (*śuddhavidyā-tattva*): *oṃ hāṃ śaṅkarāya namaḥ*.
On the right side: *oṃ hāṃ māyā-tattvāya namaḥ*.
To the Lord of the principle of Māyā: *oṃ hāṃ gahaneśāya namaḥ*. (l. 7)
On the left side: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of time (kālatattva).
To the lord of the principle of time: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Kālanābha. Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the principle of necessity (niyati-tattva).
To the Lord of the Principle of Necessity: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Body of Restriction.
(i.36a, f.1b, l.1) In the heart: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Principle of Limited Agency.
To the Lord of the Kalā-tattva: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Jñānabandhu.
On the chest: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the Vidyā-tattva. To the Lord of the Vidyā-tattva: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vedivijñāna.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of passion (rāga-tattva). To the lord of the principle of passion—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Bestower of Desire (kāmadāya).
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the person (puruṣa-tattva).

To the Lord of the principle of Puruṣa: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the subtle body. (l. 3) At the heart: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of Prakṛti. To the Lord of the principle of Prakṛti: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Pradhāna.
In the abdomen—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Guṇatattva. To the Lord of Guṇatattva—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Trideha.
In the spinal column—oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Buddhitattva.
To the Lord of the principle of intellect (buddhi-tattva): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Buddhi. In the center of the navel: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to the principle of ego (ahaṅkāra-tattva).
To the Lord of the principle of ego: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Ahaṅkāra-kṛti.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of mind (manastattva).
To the lord of the principle of mind—oṃ hāṃ, homage to volition (saṃkalpa).
At the three joints—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of hearing (śrotratattva).
To the Lord of the principle of hearing: *oṃ hāṃ vyomacāriṇe namaḥ*—on the two ears.

*oṃ hāṃ tvaktatvāya namaḥ*; to the Lord of the principle of touch: *oṃ hāṃ sarvāṅgāya namaḥ*—on the skin. *oṃ hāṃ cakṣustatvāya namaḥ*; to the Lord of the principle of sight: *oṃ hāṃ prakāśāya namaḥ*—on the eye.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the tongue; to the lord of the principle of the tongue— oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mahāvaktra— at the tongue.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the nose (nāsatattva); homage to the lord of the principle of the nose—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Vilambaka—at the nose.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of speech (vāktattva); homage to the lord of the principle of speech—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Dundubha—at the mouth.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the hand (pāṇitattva); homage to the lord of the principle of the hand—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Samada—at the hands.

Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the feet (pādatattva); [homage] to its presiding lord—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ramaṇa—at the two feet. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the anus (pāyutattva); [homage] to its presiding lord—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Kuṇṭhakṛt—at the anus. Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of the generative organ (upasthatattva); [homage] to its presiding lord—Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ghanānanda—at the generative organ.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of sound (śabdatattva); [homage] to the lord of the principle of sound—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the subtle resonance (sūkṣmanāda)—on the head.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of touch (sparśatattva); [homage] to the lord of the principle of touch—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Balavaktra—on the forehead.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of form (rūpatattva); [homage] to the lord of the principle of form—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Bhānumati—on the mouth.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of taste (rasa-tattva); to the lord of the principle of taste—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the Water-giver—at the heart.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of smell (gandha-tattva); to the lord of the principle of smell—oṃ hāṃ, homage to the limb of smell—at the navel.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the principle of space (vyoma-tattva); to the lord of the principle of space—oṃ hāṃ, homage to Virūpākṣa—at the womb.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the wind element— homage to the lord of the wind element; Oṃ hāṃ,
homage to Mātariśvan— in that very place.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the fire-principle (agnitattva); obeisance to the lord of the fire-principle—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Tviṣānidhi—at the location within the womb (yoni).
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the water-principle (jalatattva); obeisance to the lord of the water-principle—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Jaleśa—from the womb up to the kneecaps.
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to the earth-principle (pṛthvītattva); obeisance to the lord of the earth-principle—Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śrīkaṇṭha.
In the Śiva-tattva: *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Anāśritā;
at the top of the head: *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Anāthā;
on the eastern head: *Oṃ hāṃ*, salutation to Anandā (the Endless).
On the southern crown: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vyoṃmarūpā.
(l. 4) On the northern crown: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Vyomavyāpin.
On the western crown: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ūrddhvagāmin.
In the eastern face: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Mocitā.
In the southern face: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Rocitā.
In the northern face: Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Dīpikā.
On the western face: *oṃ hāṃ iṇḍikāyai namaḥ*. On the forehead, in the principle of Śakti (*śaktitatve*): *oṃ hāṃ śāntātītāya namaḥ*.
On the right eye: *oṃ hāṃ śāktyai namaḥ*.
In the left eye: *oṃ hāṃ vidyāyai namaḥ*.
In the right ear: *oṃ hāṃ pratiṣṭhāyai namaḥ*.
In the left ear: *oṃ hāṃ nivṛttyai namaḥ*.
In the right nostril—in the principle of Sadāśiva: *oṃ hāṃ sadāśivāya namaḥ*.
In the left nostril: *oṃ hāṃ śikhaṇḍine namaḥ*.
On the right bell: *oṃ hāṃ śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ*. On the left bell: *oṃ hāṃ trimūrttaye namaḥ*.
On the upper lip: *oṃ hāṃ ekarudrāya namaḥ*.
On the lower lip: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Ekanetra.
On the upper teeth: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Śivottama.
On the lower teeth: Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣma.
At the chin—in the principle of Īśvara: *oṃ hāṃ anantāya namaḥ*.
On the tongue: *oṃ hāṃ manonmanyai namaḥ*. At the base of the throat: *oṃ hāṃ sarvabhūtadamanyai namaḥ*.
In the ear: *oṃ hāṃ balapradhanyai namaḥ*.
In the heart: *balavikaraṇyai namaḥ*. In the right breast: *oṃ hāṃ kalanikaraṇyai namaḥ*. (l. 4)
On the left breast: *oṃ hāṃ kālyai namaḥ*.
At the navel: *oṃ hāṃ raudryai namaḥ*. On the right nipple: *oṃ hāṃ jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ*.
At the touch of the left [hand], in the principle of knowledge (vidyā-tattva): Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Vāmā. At the secret place: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Aṅguṣṭhamātra.
At the right foot: Oṃ hāṃ, salutation to Īśāna.
In the left foot: *oṃ hāṃ ekeṣaṇāya namaḥ*.
In the right seed-syllable: *oṃ hāṃ ekapiṅgalāya namaḥ*. In the left seed-syllable: *oṃ hāṃ udbhavāya namaḥ*.
At the base of the right hand during the *ādhāna*: *oṃ hāṃ bhavāya namaḥ*. At the middle joint: *oṃ hāṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ*.
At the middle joint (l. 7): *oṃ hāṃ mahādrutaye namaḥ*.
At the tip of the forefinger—in the principle of Māyā: *oṃ hāṃ ekaśikhāya namaḥ*.
On the right thumb—in the principle of Kāla: *oṃ hāṃ ekavīrāya namaḥ*.
On the joint at the base of the thumb—
Oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Pañcāntaka.
On the middle joint of the thumb— in the principle of necessity (niyatitatva)— oṃ hāṃ, obeisance to Lakulīśvara.
On the tip-joint of the thumb: *oṃ hāṃ saṃvartāya namaḥ*.
On the middle joint at the base of the thumb—in the principle of Time (*kālatattva*): *oṃ hāṃ jyotiṣe namaḥ*.
On the middle joint of the thumb: *oṃ hāṃ caṇḍāya namaḥ*.
In the middle joint of the tip of the right thumb—in the principle of Pure Knowledge (śuddhavidyā-tattva)—*oṃ hāṃ krodhanāya namaḥ*.
On the right index finger—*oṃ hāṃ ekaśikhāya namaḥ*.
In the middle joint at the base of the right index finger—*oṃ hāṃ ānandāntāya namaḥ*.
On the middle joint of the right index finger: *oṃ hāṃ ajāya namaḥ*.
On the tip-joint of the right index finger: *oṃ hāṃ umāpataye namaḥ*.
In the middle of the root-joint of the index finger, [pertaining to] the principle of passion (*rāgatatva*): *oṃ hāṃ pracaṇḍāya namaḥ*.
At the middle joint of the left index finger: *oṃ hāṃ ekavīrāya namaḥ*.
At the tip of the left index finger: *oṃ hāṃ īśānāya namaḥ*.
On the right middle finger: *oṃ hāṃ bhavāya namaḥ*.
On the middle root-joint: *oṃ hāṃ mṛgāya namaḥ*.
On each of the middle joints: *oṃ hāṃ bhīmāya namaḥ*.
On the middle tip-joint, in the principle of Puruṣa (*puruṣatattva*): *oṃ hāṃ vāmāya namaḥ*.
In the middle of the middle joint of the ring finger: *oṃ hāṃ śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ*.
In the middle of the middle joint [of the middle finger]: *oṃ hāṃ aumāya namaḥ*. (l.
7) In the middle of the upper joint of the middle finger: *oṃ hāṃ kaumārāya namaḥ*.
On the right ring finger—Oṃ Hāṃ, salutation to Brahmā.
On the base joint of the ring finger—salutation to Viṣṇu.
On the middle joint of the ring finger...
Svāhā to the reality of the syllable *haṃ*.
Svāhā to the lord of the reality of the syllable *haṃ*, to the one who has made the sound *haṃ*.
Svāhā to the principle of mind;
svāhā to Saṅkalpa, the lord of the principle of mind;
svāhā to the principle of hearing.
To the Lord of the Reality of the Hearers—*vyomacāra*, svāhā!
To the Reality of Reality, svāhā!
To the Lord of the Reality of Reality—*sarvāṅga*, svāhā!
To the principle of the eye, svāhā!
To the lord of the principle of the eye—Light, svāhā!
To the principle of the tongue, svāhā!
To the Lord of the principle of the tongue—Mahāvaktra, svāhā! To the principle of the nose, svāhā! To the Lord of the principle of the nose—Viluṇḍaka, svāhā!
Svāhā to the principle of speech;
svāhā to the Lord of the principle of speech, Vibhu;
svāhā to the principle of the feet.
To the Lord of the reality of the feet— to Ramaṇeśa— svāhā!
To the reality of the hands, svāhā!
To the lord of the state of being a hand—Sāmagāya svāhā!
To the state of being a hundred thousand—svāhā!
To the lord of the state of being a hundred thousand, who acts as a leprosy—svāhā!
Svāhā to the state of being present; svāhā to the overlord of the state of being present—the one who is intense bliss; svāhā to the state of being Śa...śata.
To the Lord of the element of sound—Sūkṣmanāda, svāhā!
To the element of touch, svāhā!
To the Lord of the element of touch—Balavaktra, svāhā!
Svāhā to the reality of form. Svāhā to Bhānumat, the lord of the reality of form.
Svāhā to the reality of taste.
To the Lord of the principle of taste—the one who bestows water—svāhā!
To the principle of smell, svāhā!
To the Lord of the principle of smell—the one whose limb is fragrance—svāhā!
Svāhā to the principle of space.
Svāhā to Sūkṣma, the lord of the principle of space.
